G5000.d:
Ταβειθά (Rec. Ταβιθά), ἡ (Aram. טַבְיְתָא or טְבִיתָא), 
 Tabitha: Acts.9:36, 40 (cf. Δορκάς).†
 (AS)

G5001.d:
τάγμα, -τος, τό
 (τάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּגֶל, also for חַי, רַגְלִי ;] 
that which has been arranged or placed in order; esp. as military term, a company, troop, division, rank: metaphorically, 1 Cor.15:23 (see ICC, in l).†
 (AS)

G5002.d:
τακτός, -ή, -όν
 (τάσσω), [in LXX: Job.12:5 (שַׁאֲנָן) * ;] 
ordered, fixed, stated: ἡμέρα, Acts.12:21,†
 (AS)

G5003.d:
ταλαιπωρέω, -ῶ
 (ταλαίπωρος), [in LXX Chiefly for שָׁדַד pu. ;] 
  1. to do hard labour, suffer hardship or distress: Jas.4:9. 
  2. In cl. occasionally trans., to weary, distress (so Ps.17:9, Isa.33:1).†
 (AS)

G5004.d:
ταλαιπωρία, -ας, ἡ
 (ταλαίπωρος) [in LXX chiefly for שֹׁד ;] 
  1. hard work (Hippocr.). 
  2. hardship, suffering, distress: Rom.3:16 (LXX) pl., Jas.5:1 (see B1., § 32, 6; WM, 220; Swete, Mk., 153). 
 (Hdt., Thuc., al.; and cf. MM, xxiv.)†
 (AS)

G5005.d:
ταλαίωρος, -ον 
 [in LXX: Ps.137:8 (שָׁדַד), Isa.33:1 (ποιεῖν τ., שָׁדַד), Tob.13:10, Wis.3:11, al. ;] 
distressed, miserable, wretched: Rom.7:24, Rev.3:17.†
 (AS)

G5006.d:
ταλαντιαῖος, -α, -ον
 (τάλαντον), 
  (a) worth a talent; 
  (b) of a talent's weight: Rev.16:21.†
 (AS)

G5007.d:
τάλαντομ, -ον, τ 
 [in LXX for כִּכָּר ;] 
  1. a balance (Hom.). 
  2. that which is weighed, a talent; 
  (a) a talent in weight (in Horn. always of gold); 
  (b) a sum of money, whether gold or silver, equivalent to a talent in weight (see DB, iii, 418 ff.): Matt.18:24 25:15 ff.†
 (AS)

G5008.d:
ταλειθά (Rec. ταλιθά), (Aram. טְלִיתָא, see Dalman, Gr., 150), 
 talitha, i.e. maiden: Mark.5:41.†
 (AS)

G5009.d:
ταμεῖον
 (late syncopated form of cl. ταμιεῖον; see M, Pr., 44 f.; Bl., § 6, 5; Thackeray, Gr., 63 ff.; Deiss., BS, 182 f.), -ον, τό, [in LXX chiefly for חֶדֶר ;] 
  1. a treasury (Thuc., al). 
  2. a store-chamber (Arist., Xen.; Deu.28:8): Luke.12:24. 
  3. an inner chamber (Xen., Hell., v, 4, 5 Isa.26:20, al.): Matt.6:6 24:26, Luke.12:3.†
 (AS)

G5010.d:
τάξις, -εως, ἡ
 (τάσσω), [in LXX: Job.38:12 (מָקוֹם), Ps.110:4 (דִּבְרָה), 2Ma.9:18, al. ;] 
  1. an arranging, hence, in military sense, disposition of an army, battle array (Thuc., al.). 
  2. arrangement, order (Plat., al): Luke.1:8. 
  3. due order: Col.2:5 (ICC, in l); κατὰ τάξιν, 1 Cor.14:40. 
  4. office, order (for exx., see MM, xxiv): Heb.5:6 (LXX), Heb.5:6 6:20 7:11, 17" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G5011.d:
ταπεινός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX for שָׁפָל, עָנִי, etc. ;] 
low-lying; metaphorically, 
  (a) lowly, of low degree, brought low: Jas.1:9, 2 Cor.7:6 (cf. Sir.25:23); οἱ τ., opposite to δυνάσται, Luke.1:52; τ. ταπεινοῖς (neut., R, txt.; masc., R, mg.; see ICC, in l), Rom.12:16; 
  (b) lowly in spirit, humble, in cl. usually in a slighting sense (see Tr., Syn., § xlii; but see also Abbott, Essays, 81), in NT in an honourable sense: 2 Cor.10:1; before τ. καρδίᾳ, Matt.11:29 (cf. Ps.34:19); opposite to ὑπερήφανος, Jas.4:6, 1 Pet.5:5" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G5012.d:
ταπεινοφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ
 (ταπεινόφρων) 
lowliness of mind, humility: Acts.20:19, Eph.4:2, Phil.2:3, Col.3:12, 1 Pet.5:5; of a false humility, Col.2:18, 23 (rare outside of NT, but found in bad sense in FlJ, BJ, iv, 9, 2; also in Epictet., see Tr., Syn., § xlii).†
 (AS)

G5013.d:
ταπεινόω, -ῶ
 (ταπεινός), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָה, also for שָׁפֵל, כָּנַע, etc. ;] 
to make low: ὄρος (βουνόν), Luke.3:5 (LXX). Metaphorical, to humble, abase: Matt.18:4 23:12, Luke.14:11 18:14, 2 Cor.11:7 12:21, Phil.2:8; pass., Matt.23:12, Luke.14:11 18:14, Phil.4:12; id. with mid. sense, Jas.4:10, 1 Pet.5:6.†
 (AS)

G5014.d:
ταπείνωσις, -εως, ἡ
 (ταπεινόω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי ;] 
abasement, humiliation, low estate: Luke.1:48, Acts.8:33" (LXX), Phil.3:21, Jas.1:10 (Plat., Arist., and later writers).†
 (AS)

G5015.d:
ταράσσω 
 [in LXX for בָּהַל, רָגַז, etc., forty-six words in all ;] 
to disturb, trouble, stir up: primarily in physical sense (Hom., Eur.): τ. ὕδωρ, John.1:5 [4], John.1:7. Metaphorical, of the mind (Æsch., Plat., al.), to trouble, disquiet, perplex: Acts.15:24, Gal.1:7 5:10; ἑαυτόν (troubled himself; Westc., in l), John.11:33; of a crowd, to stir up, Acts.17:8, 13; pass., Matt.2:3 14:26, Mark.6:50, Luke.1:12 24:38, John.12:27 (Ps.6:4) Ps.14:1, 7, 1 Pet.3:14" (LXX) ; τ. πνεύματι, John.13:21 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-ταράσσω) 
 (AS)

G5016.d:
ταραχή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 (ταράσσω), [in LXX for חָלָה, מְהוּמָה, etc. ;] 
trouble, disturbance: τ. ὕδατος, John.1:5 [4]. In pl. (as in cl.), tumults: Mark.13:8, Rec.†
 (AS)

G5017.d:
τάραχος, -ου, ὁ
 (ταράσσω), [in LXX for מְהוּמָה, etc. ;] 
later form of ταραχή (Xen., al.; see Thackeray, Gr., 159): Acts.12:18 19:23.† 
 (AS)

G5019.d:
Ταρσός, -oῦ 
 Tarsus, a city of Cilicia: Acts.9:30 11:25 22:3.†
 (AS)

G5020.d:
ταρταρόω, -ῶ
 (Τάρταρος, a Greek name for the underworld, esp. the abode of the damned), 
to cast into hell: 2 Pet.2:4 (see Mayor, in l).†
 (AS)

G5021.d:
τάσσω 
 [in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם, also for צָוָה pi., נָתַן, etc. ;] 
primarily, in military sense, then generally, to draw up in order, arrange in place, assign, appoint, order: with dative (accusative) and inf. (Bl., § 72, 5), Acts.15:2 18:2 (διατ-, WH) Acts.22:10; ἑαυτούς, 1 Cor.16:15; pass., Matt.8:9 (T [WH], R, txt., om.), Luke.7:8, Rom.13:1; ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον (perh. in mid. sense; see EGT and Page, in l), Acts.13:48; mid., to appoint for oneself or by one's own authority, Matt.28:16, Acts.28:23.†
 (AS)

G5022.d:
ταῦρος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹר ;] 
a bull: Matt.22:4, Acts.14:13, Heb.9:13 10:4.†
 (AS)

G5027.d:
ταφή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 (θάπτω), [in LXX chiefly for קָבַר and cognate forms ;] 
burial: Matt.27:7 (Hdt., al.; for other meanings, see LS, see word, Deiss., BS, 355 f., MM xxiv).†
 (AS)

G5028.d:
τάφος, -ου, ὁ
 (θάντω), [in LXX chiefly for קֶבֶר ;] 
  1. a burial (Hom., al.). 
  2. a grave, tomb (Res., Hdt., al.): Matt.23:27, 29 27:61, 64 27:66 28:1, Rom.3:13" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G5029.d:
τάχα 
 (ταχύς), 
 adv., [in LXX: Wis.13:6 14:19 * ;] 
  (a) (chiefly poët.), quickly, presently; 
  (b) perhaps: Rom.5:7, Phm 15.†
 (AS)

G5030.d:
ταχέως
 (ταχύς) 
 adv., [in LXX chiefly for מְהֵרָה and cognate  forms ;] 
quickly, hastily: Luke.14:21 16:6, John.11:31, 1 Cor.4:19, Phil.2:19, 24, 2 Tim.4:9; with suggestion of rashness, Gal.1:6, 2 Thess.2:2, 1 Tim.5:22.†
 (AS)

G5031.d:
ταχινός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX: Pro.1:16, Hab.1:6, Isa.59:7 (מָהַר), Wis.13:2, Sir.11:22 18:26 * ;] 
poët. and late for ταχύς, swift: of swift approach, 2 Pet.1:14 2:1.†
 (AS)

G5032.d:
τάχειον, see: ταχύ.
 ταχύ
 (neut. of ταχύς), 
 adv., [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;] 
quickly, speedily, forthwith: Matt.5:25 28:7-8, Mark.9:39, Luke.15:22, John.11:29, Rev.2:16 3:11 11:14 22:7, 12 22:2 o. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (see Bl., § 44, 3): John.13:27 20:4, 1 Tim.3:14 (T, Rec.), Heb.13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Acts.17:15.†
 (AS)

G5033.d:
τάχιστα, see: ταχύ.
 ταχύ
 (neut. of ταχύς), 
 adv., [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;] 
quickly, speedily, forthwith: Matt.5:25 28:7-8, Mark.9:39, Luke.15:22, John.11:29, Rev.2:16 3:11 11:14 22:7, 12 22:2 o. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (see Bl., § 44, 3): John.13:27 20:4, 1 Tim.3:14 (T, Rec.), Heb.13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Acts.17:15.†
 (AS)

G5034.d:
τάχος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of מָהַר ;] 
swiftness, speed. Adverbially, ἐν τ. (ταχέως), quickly, speedily, soon: Luke.18:8, Acts.12:7 22:18 25:4, Rom.16:20, 1 Tim.3:14, Rev.1:1 22:6.†
 (AS)

G5035.d:
ταχύ
 (neut. of ταχύς), 
 adv., [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;] 
quickly, speedily, forthwith: Matt.5:25 28:7-8, Mark.9:39, Luke.15:22, John.11:29, Rev.2:16 3:11 11:14 22:7, 12 22:2 o. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (see Bl., § 44, 3): John.13:27 20:4, 1 Tim.3:14 (T, Rec.), Heb.13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Acts.17:15.†
 (AS)

G5036.d:
ταχύς, -εῖα, -ύ 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;] 
quick, swift, speedy: opposite to βραδύς, Ja 119.†
 (AS)

G5037.d:
τέ, 
enclitic copulative particle (= Lat. -que as καί = and, ac, atque, not very frequently in NT, more than two-thirds of the occurrences being in Ac.  
  1. τέ solitarium, and, denoting a closer affinity than καί between words and sentences which it connects (BL, §77, 8): Matt.28:12, John.4:42, Acts.2:33, 37 40 10:22 11:21, al. 
  2. Denoting a closer connection than simple καί, τὲ . . . καί, τὲ καί, τὲ . . . τέ (Acts.26:16 Rom.14:8), as well . . . as also, both . . . and: Luke.12:45, Acts.1:1 15:9, 21:30, al.; τὲ . . . δέ, and . . . and, Acts.19:2; τὲ γάρ . . . ὁμοίως δὲ καί, Rom.1:26, 27.
 (AS)

G5038.d:
τεῖχος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for חוֹמָה ;] 
a wall, esp. that about a town: Acts.9:25, 2 Cor.11:33, Heb.11:30, Rev.21:12-19 †
 (AS)

G5039.d:
τεκμήριον, -ου, τό
 (τέκμαρ, a mark, sign), [in LXX: Wis.5:4 19:13, 3Ma.3:24 * ;] 
a sure sign, a positive proof: Acts.1:1-26 (for exx., see MM, xxiv).†
 SYN.: ἔνδειγμα, q.v  (AS)

G5040.d:
τεκνίον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of τέκνον), 
a little child: as a term of endearment, in voc. pl., John.13:33, Gal.4:19, 1 John.2:1 Jn 2:12 Jn 2:28 Jn 3:7 Jn 3:13 Jn 4:4 Jn 5:21.†
 (AS)

G5041.d:
τεκνογονέω, -ῶ 
 to beget or bear children: 1 Tim.5:14 (Anthol.).†
 (AS)

G5044.d:
τεκνο-τροφέω, -ῶ 
 to rear young (of bees, Arist.), 
 to bring up children: 1 Tim.5:10.†
 (AS)

G5045.d:
τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for חָרָשׁ ;] 
an artificer in wood, stone or metal, but esp. a carpenter (see MM, xxiv): Matt.13:55, Mark.6:3.†
 (AS)

G5046.d:
τέλειος, -α, -ον
 (τέλος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלֵם, תָּמִים and cogn. forms ;] 
having reached its end, finished, mature, complete, perfect; 
  1. of persons, primarily of physical development, 
  (a) full-grown, mature: Heb.5:14; ethically: Phil.3:15; opposite to νήπιος (-άζειν), 1 Cor.2:6 14:20, Eph.4:13; τ. καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι, Col.4:12; τ. ἐν Χριστῷ, Col.1:28; 
  (b) complete, perfect (expressing the simple idea of complete goodness, without reference either to maturity or to the philosophical idea of a τέλος; see Hort on Jas.1:4): Matt.5:48 19:21, Jas.1:4 3:2; of God, Matt.5:48. 
  2. Of things, complete, perfect: Rom.12:2; ἔργον, Jas.1:4; νόμος, Jas.1:25; δώρημα, Jas.1:17; ἀγάπη, 1 John.4:18; τὸ τ., 1 Cor.13:10; compar., τελειοτέρα (σκηνή), Heb.9:11. 
 (There is probably no reference in St. Paul's usage to the use of this term in the ancient mysteries; cf. ICC on Col.1:28; but see also Lft., in l, and Notes, 173 f.) † 
 SYN.: see: ὁλόκληρος (and cf. Rendall, He., 158 ff.)  (AS)

G5047.d:
τελειότης, -ητος, ἡ
 (τέλειος), [in LXX: Jdg.9:16, 19 (תָּמִים), Pro.11:3 (תֻּמָּה), Wis.6:15 12:17, Jer.2:2 * ;] 
perfection, completeness: Col.3:14, Heb.6:1 
 (AS)

G5048.d:
τελειόω, -ῶ
 (τέλειος), [in LXX: Exod.29:9, Lev.4:5, al. (τ. χεῖρ מָלֵא pi.), 2Ki.22:26, al. (תָּמַם), Wis.4:13, al. (cf. Westc., He., 64) ;] 
  1. bring to an end, finish, accomplish, fulfil: John.4:34, Acts.20:24; of time, Luke.2:43, John.5:36 17:4; pass., ἡ γραφή, John.19:28. 
  2. to bring to maturity or completeness, to complete, perfect; 
  (a) of things: Heb.7:19, Jas.2:22, 1 John.2:5 Jn 4:12 Jn 4:17 : 
  (b) of persons, in ethical and spiritual sense: Heb.2:10 9:9 10:1, 14; pass., Luke.13:32, John.17:23, Phil.3:12, Heb.5:9 7:28 11:40 12:23, 1 John.4:18 (for a different view of the meaning in Heb.2:10, al., see Rendall, in l).†
 (AS)

G5049.d:
τελείως
 (τέλειος), 
 adv., [in LXX: Jdth.11:6, 2Ma.12:42, 3Ma.3:26 3Mac 7:22, R* ;] 
completely, perfectly: 1 Pet.1:13.†
 (AS)

G5050.d:
τελείωσις, -εως, ἡ
 (τελειόω), [in LXX chiefly for מִלֻּא, Exod.29:22, al. ;] 
fulfilment, completion, perfection: Luke.1:45, Heb.7:11.†
 (AS)

G5051.d:
τελειωτής, -οῦ, ὁ
 (τελειόω), 
a consummator, finisher: Heb.12:2 (nowhere else).†
 (AS)

G5052.d:
τελεσφορέω, -ῶ
 (τέλος, φέρω) [in LXX: 4Ma.13:20 * ;] 
  (a) of  plants, to bring fruit to perfection (Theophr.): Luke.8:14 
  (b) of females, to bear perfect offspring (Artemid.; 4Mac, l.with).†
 (AS)

G5053.d:
τελευτάω, -ῶ
 (τελευτή), [in LXX chiefly for מוּת ;] 
  1. trans., to complete, finish; esp. τ. τ. αἰῶνα, τ. βίον, to complete life, to die (Æsch., Hdt., al.). 
  2. Intrans., to come to an end, hence, to die (Hdt., al.): Matt.2:19 9:18 22:25, Mark.9:48, Luke.7:2, John.11:39, Acts.2:29 7:15, Heb.11:22; Hebraistically, θανάτῳ τελευτάτω (מוּת, Exod.21:17), Matt.15:4, Mark.7:10" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G5054.d:
τελευτή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (τελέω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּת, מָוֶת ;] 
  1. a finishing. 
  2. an end: τ. βίου (Hdt., al.): also without βίου, the end of life, death (Hdt., Plat., al.): Matt.2:15.†
 (AS)

G5055.d:
τελέω, -ῶ
 (τέλος), [in LXX for כָּלָה, pi., etc. ;] 
  1. to bring to an end, complete, finish: τ. δρόμον, 2 Tim.4:7; τ. λόγους, Matt.7:28 19:1 26:1; τ. παραβολάς, Matt.13:53; τ. πόλεις, Matt.10:23; pass., Rev.15:8 20:3, 5 20:7; with ptcp., Matt.11:1. 
  2. to execute, perform, complete, fulfil: Luke.2:39, Acts.13:29, Rom.2:27, 2 Cor.12:9, Gal.5:16, Jas.2:8, Rev.11:7; pass., Luke.12:50 18:31 22:37, John.19:28, 30, Rev.10:7 15:1 17:17. 
  3. to pay (frequently in cl.): Matt.17:24, Rom.13:6 
 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, συν-τελέω).†
 (AS)

G5056.d:
τέλος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX for קֵץ, etc.; εἰς τὸ τ., chiefly for נֶצַח and cognate forms ;] 
  1. end: most frequently of the termination or limit of an act or state (in NT also of the end of a period of time, cl. τελευτή), Luke.1:33, 1 Cor.10:11, 2 Cor.3:13, 1 Pet.4:7; by meton., of one who makes an end, Rom.10:4; ἕως (ἄχρι, μέκρι) τέλους, 1 Cor.1:8, 2 Cor.1:13, Heb.3:14 6:11, Rev.2:26; εἰς τ., to or at the end, Matt.10:22, Mark.13:13, Luke.18:5, John.13:1 (or here, to the uttermost, see Westc., in l); τ. ἔχειν, Luke.22:37; adverbially, τὸ δὲ τέλος, finally, 1 Pet.3:8; of the last in a series, Rev.21:6 22:13; of the issue, fate or destiny, Matt.26:58; with genitive of thing(s), Rom.6:21, al.; with genitive of person(s), 2 Cor.11:13, al.; of the aim or purpose, 1 Tim.1:5. 
  2. toll, custom, revenue: Rom.13:7; pl., as most usually, Matt.17:25 
 (AS)

G5057.d:
τελώνης, -ου, ὁ
 (τέλος, ὠνέομαι) 
  1. a farmer of taxes (Let. publicanus). 
  2. A subordinate of the former, who collected taxes or tolls in a particular district, a tax-gatherer (EV, publican): Matt.5:46 10:3, Luke.3:12 5:27, 29 7:29 18:10-11, 13; pl., τ. κ. ἁμαρτωλοί, Matt.9:10-11 11:19, Mark.2:15-16, Luke.5:30 7:34 15:1; τ. κ. πόρναι, Matt.21:31-32; ὁ ἐθνικὸς κ. ὁ τ., Matt.18:17 (cf. DB, iv, 172; ext., 394 f.; MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G5058.d:
τελώνιον, -ου, τό
 (τελώνης), 
a custom house (so in MGr.), tollhouse, place of toll: Matt.9:9, Mark.2:14, Luke.5:27.†
 (AS)

G5059.d:
τέρας, -ατος, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for מוֹפֵת ;] 
a wonder, marvel: in NT always pl., τ. κ. σημεῖα, Matt.24:24, al. (see: σημεῖον) 
 (AS)

G5062.d:
τεσσεράκοντα (Rec. τεσσαρ-, v, WH, App., 150; M, Pr., 45 f.;  Thackeray, Gr., 62 f., 73 f.), οἱ, αἱ, τά, indecl., 
 forty: Matt.4:2, Mark.1:13, Luke.4:2, John.2:20, Acts.1:3, al 
 (AS)

G5063.d:
τεσσερακονταετίς
 (Τ, -έτης; Rec. τεσσαρ-, see supr.), -ές 
of forty years, forty years old: Acts.7:23 13:18.†
 (AS)

G5064.d:
τέσσαρες
 (and Ion. and late -ερεν, and late accusative -εν; see WH, App., 150; M, Pr., 36, 45 f.), οἱ, αἱ, -αρα, τά, genitive, -ων, 
four: Matt.24:31, Mark.2:3, Luke.2:37, John.11:17 19:23, Acts.10:11, Rev.4:4, 6, al 
 (AS)

G5066.d:
τεταρταῖος, -α, -ον
 (τέταρτος), [in LXX: 2Ki.3:4 A (רְבִיעִי) * ;] 
of or on the fourth day: τ. εἶναι (Hdt., τ. γενέσθαι), to be four days dead, John.11:39.†
 (AS)

G5067.d:
τέταρτος, -η, -ον 
 [in LXX chiefly for רְבִיעִי ;] 
fourth: Matt.14:25, Mark.6:48, Acts.10:30, Rev.4:7 6:7-8 8:12 16:8 21:19.†
 (AS)

G5068.d:
τετράγωνος, -ον
 (τετρα-, see supr., + γωνία), [in LXX for רָבַע and cogn. forms ;] 
square: Rev.21:16 (Hdt., Plat., al.).†
 (AS)

G5069.d:
τετράδιον, ου, τό 
 a quarternion, a group of four: στρατιωτῶν, Acts.12:4 (Philo). 
 (AS)

G5070.d:
τετρακισ-χίλιοι, -αι, -α 
 four thousand: Matt.15:38 16:10, Mark.8:9, 20, Acts.21:38.†
 (AS)

G5072.d:
τετράμηνος, -ον 
 [in LXX (neut.): Jdg.19:2 A Jdg.20:47 A (עַרְבָּעָה חֳדָשִׁים ) * ;] 
of four months, four months; as subst., τ. (sc. ὥρα, but neut. in Rec.), John.4:35 (Thuc., al.).†
 (AS)

G5074.d:
τετρά-πους, -ουν 
 [in LXX chiefly for בְּהֵמָה ;] 
four-footed: of beasts, neut. pl., Acts.10:12 11:6, Rom.1:23.†
 (AS)

G5075.d:
τετρααρχέω (Rec. τετραρχ-; see WH, App., 145), -ῶ 
 (τετραάρχης), 
to be tetrarch: with genitive, Luke.3:1 (FlJ, BJ, iii, 10, 7).†
 (AS)

G5076.d:
τετραάρχης (Rec. τετράρχης, see supr.), -ου, ὁ 
 (τετρα- in corp. = τέτορα, Doric for τέσσαρα, + ἄρχω), 
a tetrarch, i.e. 
  (a) prop., the governor of a fourth part of a region (Strab.); 
  (b) any petty ruler (Plut.); in NT, of Herod Antipas: Matt.14:1, Luke.3:19 9:7, Acts.13:1.†
 (AS)

G5077.d:
τεφρόω, -ῶ
 (τέφρα, ashes; Wis.2:3, al.), 
to burn to ashes: 2 Pet.2:6.†
 (AS)

G5078.d:
τέχνη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX for חׇכְמָה, מַעֲשֶׂה, עֲבֹדָה ;] 
art, craft, trade: Acts.17:29 18:3, Rev.18:22 (WH, R, mg., om.).†
 (AS)

G5079.d:
τεχνίτης, -ου, ὁ
 (τέχνη), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;] 
a craftsman, artificer: Acts.19:24, 38, Rev.18:22; of God (Wis.13:1), Heb.11:10.†
 SYN.: δημιουργός, which see, and cf. Tr., Syn., § cv  (AS)

G5080.d:
τήκω 
 [in LXX for מָסַס ni., מָקַק ni., מוּג ni., etc. ;] 
trans., 
 to melt, melt down; pass., to melt, melt away: 2 Pet.3:12.†
 (AS)

G5081.d:
τηλαυγῶς 
 adv. (τῆλε, afar, + αὐγή, radiance), poët. and in late prose, 
at a distance clearly: Mark.8:25 (W, mg., δηλαυγῶς).†
 (AS)

G5082.d:
τηλικοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
 (altern. of τηλικόσδε, -ήδε, -όνδε, strength­ened form of τηλίκος), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:3, 3Ma.3:9, 4Ma.16:4 * ;] 
  1. of persons, 
  (a) of such an age, so old; 
  (b) so young. 
  2. Of things, so great: 2 Cor.1:10, Heb.2:3, Jas.3:4, Rev.16:18.†
 (AS)

G5083.d:
τηρέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, etc. ;] 
  1. to watch over, guard, keep, preserve: Matt.27:36, Acts.16:23, al.; ἑαυτόν, 2 Cor.11:9, 1 Tim.5:22, Jas.1:27, Ju 21; before εἰς, John.12:7, Acts.25:21, 1 Pet.1:4, 2 Pet.2:4 2:9 3:7, Ju 6; ἐν, John.17:11-12, Ju 21; ἐκ, John.17:15, Rev.3:10; τ. πίστιν, 2 Tim.4:7, Rev.14:12; τ. ἑνότητα τ. πνεύματος, Eph.4:3. 
  2. to watch, give heed to, observe: τ. σάββατον, John.9:16; τ. ἐντολήν (-άς), Matt.19:17, John.14:15 15:10, 1 Tim.6:14, 1 John.2:3-4 Jn 3:22 Jn 3:24 Jn 5:3, Rev.12:17 14:12; τ. λόγον (-ους), John.8:51-52, 55 14:23-24 15:20 17:6, 1 John.2:5, Rev.3:8, 10 22:7, 9; τ. νόμον, Acts.15:5, Jas.2:10; τ. παράδοσιν, Mark.7:9; τ. ἔργα, Rev.2:26; τ. γεγραμμένα, Rev.1:3 (cf. δια-, παρα-, συν-τηρέω) 
 SYN.: φυλάσσω, implying custody and protection: τ. expresses the idea of watchful care and "may mark the result of which φ. is the means" (Thayer see word)  (AS)

G5084.d:
τήρησις, -εως, ἡ
 (τηρέω), [in LXX: Wis.6:18, (Sir.32:23), 1Ma.5:18, 2Ma.3:40, 3Ma.5:44 * ;] 
  1. a watching, hence, imprisonment, ward (see Deiss., BS, 267): Acts.4:3 5:18. 
  2. a keeping: τ. ἐντολῶν (cf. Sir, Wis, ll. with, and see Westc. on 1 John.2:3.), 1 Cor.7:19.†
 (AS)

G5085.d:
Τιβεριάς, -άδος, ἡ 
 (Τιβέριος), 
Tiberias, a city of Galilee: John.6:23, John.6:1 21:1 (cf Γεννησσαρέτ, Γαλιλαία).† 
 (AS)

G5086.d:
Τιβέριος, -ου, ὁ, 
 the Emperor Tiberius: Luke.3:1.†
 (AS)

G5087.d:
τίθημι, 
 [in LXX for שִׁית ,נתן ,שׂוּם, etc. ;] 
  1. causative of κεῖμαι, 
  (a) to place, lay, set: Luke.6:48, Rom.9:33, al.; of laying the dead to rest, Mark.15:47, Luke.23:55, John.11:34, Acts.7:16, al.; before ἐπί, with genitive, Luke.8:16, John.19:19, al.; id. with accusative, Mark.4:21, 2 Cor.3:13, al.; ὑπό, Matt.5:15, al.; παρά, Acts.4:35, 37. Mid., to have put or placed, to place for oneself: of putting in prison, Acts.4:3, 5:18, 25, al.; of giving counsel, βουλήν, Acts.27:12; of laying up in one's heart, Luke.1:66 21:14 ( 1Ki.21:12); 
  (b) to put down, lay down: of bending the knees, τ. γόνατα, to kneel, Mark.15:19, Acts.7:60, al.; of putting off garments, John.13:4; of laying down life, τ. ψυχήν, John.10:11, 15 17, 18 13:37, 38 15:13, 1 John.3:16; of laying by money, παρ ̓ ἑαυτῷ, 1 Cor.16:2; of setting on food, John.2:10; metaphorically, of setting forth an idea in symbolism, Mark.4:30. 
  2. to set, fix, establish: ὑπόδειγμα, 2 Pet.2:6. 
  3. to make, appoint: Matt.22:44, Mark.12:36, Luke.20:43, Acts.2:35, Rom.4:17, al. Mid., to make, set or appoint for oneself: Acts.20:28, 1 Cor.12:28, 1 Thess.5:9, 1 Tim.1:12, al.; before ἵνα, John.15:16 (cf . ἀνα-, προσ-ανα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἀντι-δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, συν-επι-, κατα-, συν-κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-τίθημι). 
 (AS)

G5088.d:
τίκτω 
 [in LXX chiefly for יָלַד ;] 
prop., of parents, 
 to beget, bring forth, but esp. the latter, and so always in NT: absol., Luke.1:57 2:6, John.16:21, Gal.4:27" (LXX) (see M, Pr., 127), Rev.12:2, 4; υἱόν, Matt.1:21, 23 1:25 Luke.1:31 2:7, Rev.12:5, 13; pass., Matt.2:2, Luke.2:11. Metaphorical, of the earth, βοτάνην, Heb.6:7 (Æsch., al.); of lust, ἁμαρτίαν, Jas.1:15.†
 (AS)

G5089.d:
τίλλω 
 [in LXX: Est.9:3, Isa.18:7, Dan LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) * ;] 
to pluck, pluck off: στάχυας, Matt.12:1, Mark.2:23, Luke.6:1.†
 (AS)

G5090.d:
Τιμαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. טִימַי (?), see Zorell, see word), 
 Timæus: Mark.10:46.†
 (AS)

G5091.d:
τιμάω, -ῶ
 (τιμή), [in LXX for כָּבַד pi., עָרַךְ hi., etc. ;] 
  1. to  fix the value, price: with accusative of person(s), of Christ, Matt.27:9 (LXX). 
  2. to honour: with accusative of person(s), Matt.15:4 (LXX), Matt.15:5, 8" (LXX) Matt.19:19 (LXX), Mark.7:6, 10 10:19, Luke.18:28" (LXX), John.5:23 8:49 12:26, Eph.6:2" (LXX), 1 Tim.5:3, 1 Pet.2:17; πολλαῖς τιμαῖς, Acts.28:10.†
 (AS)

G5092.d:
τιμή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX for עֵרֶךְ, יְקָר, etc. ;] 
a valuing, hence, objectively; 
  1. a price paid or received: with genitive of person(s), Matt.27:9; with genitive of thing(s), Acts.5:2-3; pl., Acts.4:34 19:19; τ. αἵματος, Matt.27:6; ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆς, 1 Cor.6:20 7:23; ὠνεῖσθαι τιμῆς ἀργυρίου, Acts.7:16. 
  2. esteem, honour: Rom.12:10 13:7, 1 Cor.12:23, 1 Tim.5:17 6:1, Heb.5:4, 1 Pet.2:7 (R, txt., preciousness, cf. Hort, in l), 1 Pet.3:7; τ. διδόναι, 1 Cor.12:24; ἔχειν, John.4:44, Heb.3:3; τ. καὶ δόξα (δ. κ. τ.), Rom.2:7, 10, 1 Tim.1:17, Heb.2:7" (LXX), Heb.2:9, 1 Pet.1:7, 2 Pet.1:17, Rev.4:9, 11 5:12-13 7:12 21:26; τ. καὶ κράτος, 1 Tim.6:16; εἰς τ., Rom.9:21, 2 Tim.2:20-21; ἐν τ., Col.2:23; 1 Thess.4:4; by meton., of marks of honour, Acts.28:10.†
 (AS)

G5093.d:
τίμιος, -α, -ον
 (τιμή), [in LXX chiefly for יָקָר ;] 
valued, hence, 
  (a) precious, costly, highly valued: primarily, of money value, λίθος, Rev.17:4 18:12, 16 21:19; pl., 1 Cor.3:12; compar., -ώτεφος, 1 Pet.1:7, Rec.; superl., -ώτατος, Rev.18:12 21:11; in extended sense, καρπός, Jas.5:7; αἷμα, 1 Pet.1:19; ἐπαγγέλματα, 2 Pet.1:4; 
  (b) held in honour, honoured, esteemed worthy: with dative, Acts.5:34; ὁ γάμος, Heb.13:4; ψυχή, Acts.20:24 (where τ. is pleonastic, see Page, in l).†
 (AS)

G5094.d:
τιμιότης, -ητος, ἡ
 (τίμιος), 
preciousness, worth: Rev.18:19 (cf. Hort on τιμή, 1 Pet.2:7).†
 (AS)

G5095.d:
Τιμόθεος, -ου, ὁ 
 Timothy: Acts.17:14-15 18:5, Rom.16:21, al. 
 (AS)

G5097.d:
τιμωρέω, -ῶ 
 (τιμή + οὖρος, a guardian) [in LXX: Eze.5:17 14:15 (שָׁכֹל pi), Wis.12:20 18:8, al. ;] 
  1. to help. 
  2. to avenge; mid., to avenge oneself on, punish (Hdt., Eur., al): act, in this sense, Acts.22:5 26:11 (see MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G5098.d:
τιμωρία, -ας, ἡ
 (τιμωρέω), [in LXX: Pro.24:22 (פִּיד), etc. ;] 
  1. help, assistance. 
  2. vengeance, punishment: Heb.10:29.†
 SYN.: κόλασις, which see, and cf. MM, xxiv  (AS)

G5099.d:
τίνω 
 [in LXX: Pro.27:12 (τ. ζημίαν, for עָנַשׁ ni.), etc. ;] 
to pay: t. δίκην (cf. Pr, l.with), to pay penalty, 2 Thess.1:9 (see M, Th., in l).†
 (AS)

G5100.d:
τις, neut., τι, genitive, τινός, 
 enclitic indefinite pron., related to interrog. τίς as πού, πως, ποτέ to ποῦ, πῶς, πότε.  
  I. As subst., 
  1. one, a certain one: Luke.9:49, John.11:1, Acts.5:25, al.; pl., τίνες, certain, some: Luke.13:1, Acts.15:1, Rom.3:8, al. 
  2. someone, anyone, something, anything: Matt.12:29, Mark.9:30, Luke.8:46, John.2:25, Acts.17:25, Rom.5:7, al.; = indef., one (French on), Mark.8:4, John.2:25, Rom.8:24, al.; pl., τινες, some, Mark.14:4, al. 
  II. II. As adj., 
  1. a certain: Matt.18:12, Luke.1:5 8:27, Acts.3:2, al.; with proper names, Mark.15:21, Luke.23:26, al.; with genitive partit., Luke.7:19, al. 
  2. some: Mrk.16:[8], John.5:14, Acts.17:21 24:24, Heb.11:40, al. 
 (AS)

G5101.d:
τίς, neut., τί, genitive, τίνος, interrog. pron., [in LXX for מָה ,מִי ;] in masc. and fem., 
 who, which, what?; in neut., which, what?, used both in direct and in indirect questions. 
  I. I. As subst., 
  1. 1. masc., fem.: τίς; who, what?, Matt.3:7 26:68; Mark.11:28, Luke.9:9, al. mult.; with genitive partit., Acts.7:52, Heb.1:5, al; before ἐκ (= genitive partit.), Matt.6:27, Luke.14:28, John.8:46; = ποῖος, Mark.4:41 6:2, Luke.19:3, Acts.17:19, al.; = πότερος (M, Pr., 77), Matt.21:31 27:17, Luke.22:27, al.; = ὅς or ὅστις (rare in cl.; cf. Bl., §50, 5; M, Pr., 93), Acts.13:25. 
  2. Neut.: τί; what?, Matt.5:47 11:7, Mark.10:3, al.; χάριν τίνος, 1 John.3:12; διὰ τί, Matt.9:11, al.; εἰς τί, Matt.14:31, al.; elliptically, ἵνα τί (sc. γένηται), why, Matt.9:5, al.; τί οὖν, Rom.3:9 6:1, 15 1 Cor.14:15, al.; τί γάρ, Rom.3:3, Phi 1:18; τί ἐμοὶ (ὑμῖν) καὶ σοί, see: ἔγω. 
  II. As adj.: who? what? which?, Matt.5:46, Luke.14:31, John.2:18, al. 
  III. As adv.: = διὰ τι (τί ὅτι), why, Matt.6:28, Mark.4:40, Luke.6:46, John.18:23, al.; in rhet. questions, = a negation, Matt.27:4, John.21:22, 23 1 Cor.5:12 7:16, al. in exclamations (like Heb. מָה), how (2Ki.6:20, Ps.3:2, al.), Luke.12:49.
 (AS)

G5102.d:
τίτλος, -ου, ὁ 
 (Lat. titulus), [in Aq., Sm., Th.: Jer.21:4 * ;] 
a title, inscription: John.19:19-20 (in Christian Inscr., epitaph, see MM. xxiv).†
 (AS)

G5103.d:
Τίτος, -ου, ὁ 
 Titus; 
  1. St. Paul's disciple and companion: 2 Cor.2:13 7:6 7:13-14 8:6 8:16 8:23 12:18, Gal.2:1, 3, 2 Tim.4:10, Titus.1:4, subscr., Rec. (Τῖτος). 
  2. One surnamed Justus: Acts.18:7, RV (T, WH, Τίτιος).†
 (AS)

G5104.d:
1. enclit. Particle, serving to express belief in an assertion, let me tell you, surely, verily , used to express an inference, then, consequently , (Homer); and in [variant datesTragica Adespota, to introduce a general sentiment. 
2. to strengthen other Particles, γάρ τοι, ἤτοι, καίτοι, μέντοι, τοιγάρτοι, etc.: compare τἆρα, τἄν, μεντἄν. (ML)

G5105.d:
τοι-γαρ-οῦν 
 an inferential particle, [in LXX: Job.22:10 24:22, Sir.41:16, al. ;] 
wherefore then, so therefore: 1 Thess.4:8, Heb.12:1 (Hat., Plat., al.).†
 (AS)

G5106.d:
τοί-νυν 
 an inferential particle, [in LXX: Isa.3:10 5:13 27:4, Wis.1:11 8:9, a1. * ;] 
accordingly, therefore: as in cl., after the first word in a sentence, 1 Cor.9:26; accusative to later usage, at the beginning, Luke.20:25, Heb.13:13.†
 (AS)

G5107.d: antecedent to οἷος, as ἀοιδοῦ τοιοῦδ᾽ οἷος ὅδ᾽ ἐστί of such a  minstrel as is this one, (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, ἀλλ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ τοιόσδε here am I such as you see , (Odyssey by Homer):—;also, so great, so noble, so bad , τοιάδε λαίφη such  clothes, i. e. so bad , (Odyssey by Homer); τοσόσδε καὶ τοιόσδε (Herdotus Historicus):—;also with a qualifying word, τοιόσδ᾽ ἠμὲν δέμας ἠδὲ καὶ ἔργα such  both in form and works, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with the Art., ὁ τ. ἀνήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; οἱ τοιοίδε (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε in such  circumstances, (Herdotus Historicus):—;the sense is made more indefinite in τοιόσδε τις such a  one, (Thucydides):—;neuter plural τοιάδε as follows , τοιαῦτα as aforesaid , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G5108.d:
τοιοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
 (as usually in Att.. prose. Ep. and Ion. neut. -οῦτον in Al., Acts.21:25, Rec. only), 
correlat. of οἷος, ὁποῖος, ὥς, etc., 
 such as this, of such a kind, such: Matt.9:8 18:5, Mark.4:33 6:2 7:13 9:37 (T, τούτων), John.9:16, Acts.16:24, 1 Cor.5:1 11:16, 2 Cor.3:4 3:12 12:3, Heb.7:26 8:1 12:3 13:16, Jas.4:16; οἷος . . . τ., 1 Cor.15:48, 2 Cor.10:11; id. pleonast. (see Bl., § 50, 4), Mark.13:19; before ὁποῖος, Acts.26:29; ὥς, Phm 9. As subst., anarth: pl., Luke.9:9; with art., ὁ τ., such a one (Bl., § 47, 9; Ellic. on Gal.5:21): Acts.22:22, 1 Cor.5:5, al.; pl., Matt.19:14, Mark.10:14, al.; neut. pl., Acts.19:25, Rom.1:32, al 
 (AS)

G5109.d:
τοῖχος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for קִיר ;] 
a wall, esp. of a house: figuratively, Acts.23:3 (cf. τεῖχος).†
 (AS)

G5110.d:
τόκος, -ου, ὁ
 (τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ, etc. ;] 
  (a) a bringing forth, birth; 
  (b) offspring. Metaphorical, of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury (cf. Merch. of Venice, I, iii, "a breed of barren metal "): Matt.25:27, Luke.19:23 (Soph., Plat., al.).†
 (AS)

G5111.d:
τολμάω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Job.15:12 (לָקַח), Est.1:18 7:5 (לֵב מָלֵא) Jdth.14:13, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:21 R, 4Ma.8:18 * ;] 
to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold: absol, 2 Cor.11:21; before ἐπί, 2 Cor.10:2; with inf.  (Bl., § 69, 4), Matt.22:46, Mark.12:34, Luke.20:40, John.21:12, Acts.5:13 7:32, Rom.15:18, 1 Cor.6:1, 2 Cor.10:12, Phil.1:14, Ju 9; to submit to (in cl. usually absol. in this sense), Rom.5:7 (see Field, Notes, 155); τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν, took courage and went in (see Field, op. cit., 44), Mark.15:43 (cf. ἀπο-τολμάω).†
 (AS)

G5112.d:
τολμηρῶς 
 adv., (τολμηρός, bold, daring), 
boldly: compar., -ότερως (T, Rec. -ότερον), Rom.15:15.†
 (AS)

G5113.d:
τολμητής, -οῦ, ὁ 
 (τολμάω), 
a bold, daring man: 2 Pet.2:10 (Thuc.).†
 (AS)

G5115.d:
τόξον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for קֶשֶׁת ;] 
a bow: Rev.6:2.†
 (AS)

G5116.d:
τοπάζιον, -ου, τό
 (and τόπαζος, ὁ), [in LXX: Exod.28:17 35:17 (Exod.39:10), Job.28:19, Eze.28:13 (פִּטְדָה), Ps.119:127 (פָּז)* ;] 
topaz: Rev.21:20 (see Swete, in l).†
 (AS)

G5117.d:
τόπος, -ου, ὁ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָקוֹם ;] 
place: Luke.4:37 10:1, 32 John.5:13 6:10, Acts.12:17, 1 Cor.1:2, al.; τ. ἅγιος (cf. Isa.60:13), Matt.24:15; ἔρημος, Matt.14:13, al.; πεδινός, Luke.6:17; ἄνυδρος (pl.), Matt.12:43, Luke.11:24; κατὰ τόπος (BV, in divers places), Matt.24:7, Mark.13:8; τραχεῖς τ., Acts.27:29; τ. διθάλασσος (which see), ib. 41; ἑτοιμάζειν τ., John.14:2, 3; ἔχειν, Rev.12:6; διδόναι, Luke.14:9; with genitive defin., τ. βασάνου, Luke.16:28; τ. καταπαύσεως, Acts.7:49; κρανίου, Matt.27:33, Mark.15:22, John.19:17; before οὗ, Rom.9:26; ὅπου, Matt.28:6, Mark.16:6, John.4:20 6:23 10:40 11:30 19:41; ἐν ᾧ, John.11:6; ἐφ ̓ ᾧ, Acts.7:33; of a place which a person or thing occupies, Rev.2:5 6:14 12:8; τ. μαχαίρας, Matt.26:52; ὁ ἴδιος τ., Acts.1:25; of a place in a book, Luke.4:17 (cf. Clem. Rom., I Co., 8, 4). Metaphorical, of condition, station, occasion, opportunity or power: Acts.25:16, Rom.12:19 15:23, Eph.4:27 (cf. Sir.38:12). 
 SYN.: χώρα (extensive), region; χωρίον (enclosed), a piece of ground. τ. is "a portion of space viewed in reference to its occupancy, or as appropriated to a thing " (Grimm-Thayer, see word). (AS)

G5118.d:

G5181.d:
1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties  βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Sparta; for the term rather regards the irregular way in which the power was gained , than the way in which it was exercised , being applied to the mild Pisistratus, but not to the despotic kings of Persia. 2. in a wider sense, the tyrant's son , or any member of his family , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;so, ἡ τύραννος was both the queen  herself or a princess , (Euripides) 
3. τύραννος, ον, as adjective kingly, royal , [variant datesTragica Adespota 
4. imperious, despotic , (Thucydides); τύραννα δρᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus)

to be sound, healthy, in good health: Luke.5:31 7:10 15:27, 3Jo.2. In Past. Epp. (as also in cl.) metaphorically, ὑ. ἐν τ. πίστει, Titus.1:13 ; τ. πίστει, τ. ἀγάπῃ, τ. ὑπομονῇ, Titus.2:2; ἡ ὑγιαίνουσα διδασκαλία, 1 Tim.1:10, 2 Tim.4:3, Titus.1:9 2:1 ; λόγοι ὑγιαίνοντες, 1 Tim.6:3, 2 Tim.1:13.†
 (AS)

G5199.d:
ὑγιής, -ές, accusative, ὑγιῆ (Attic usually -ιᾶ), 
 [in LXX for חַי, etc. ;] 
sound, whole, healthy: Matt.12:13 15:31, Jhn.5:[4], 6, 9, 11, 14, 15 7:23, Acts.4:10; before ἀπό, Mark.5:34; of words, opinions, etc. (as in cl.), metaphorically, λόγος, Titus.2:8.†
 (AS)

G5200.d:
ὑγρός, -ά, -όν, 
 [in LXX: Jdg.16:7,8 (לַח), Job.8:16 (רָשׂב), Sir.39:13 
wet, moist, opposite to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green: Luke.23:31.†
 (AS)

G5201.d:
ὑδρία, -ας, ἠ
 (ὕδωρ), [in LXX for בַּד ;] 
  1. prop., a water-pot or jar: John.2:6, 7 John 4:28.
  2. More frequently in Attic = ἄγγυς, a pot, urn or jar of any kind, as for holding wine, coins, etc. (see Rutherford, NPhr., 23; MM, xxv).
† (AS)

G5202.d:
ὑδροποτίω, -ῶ
 (ὕδωρ, πίνω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:12 שָׁתָה מַיִם) * ;] 
to drink water, opposite to οἴνῳ χρῆσθαι: 1 Tim.5:23 (Hdt., i, 71; Plat., Rep., 561 with, al.).†
 (AS)

G5203.d:
ὑδρωπικός, -ή, -όν
 (ὕδρωψ, dropsy), 
dropsical, suffering from dropsy: Luke.14:2.†
 (AS)

ὕδωρ 
 genitive, 
 ὕδατος, τό, 
 [in LXX chiefly for מַיִם ;] 
water: Matt.3:16, Mark.1:10, Luke.7:44, John.4:7, Jas.3:12, Rev.8:10, al.; pl., Matt.14:28-29, John.3:23, Rev.1:15, al.; βαπτίζειν (ἐν) ὕδατι, Matt.3:11, Mark.1:8, John.1:26, al.; τ. λυυτρὸν τοῦ ὕ., Eph.5:26; opposite to οἴνος, John.2:9 4:46; αἷμα, John.19:34, Heb.9:19, 1 John.5:6 Jn 5:8 Matt.17:15 Mark.9:22; πνεῦμα, John.1:26, 31 1:33; πνεῦμα καὶ πῦρ, Matt.3:11, Luke.3:16;ἐξ ὕ. κ. πνεύματος γεννηθῆναι, John.3:5; metaphorically, of divine truth and grace (τ.) ὕ. (τ.) ζῶν, John.4:10-11 (cf. John.4:13-15); τ. ὕ. τ. ζωῆς, of spiritual refresh­ment, Rev.21:6 22:1, 17 
 (AS)

G5205.d:
ὑετός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (ὕω, to rain), [in LXX chiefly for ;] 
rain: Acts.14:17 28:2, Heb.6:7, Jas.5:18, Rev.11:6; ὄψιμος (which see), sc. ὑ., Jas.5:7.†
 (AS)

G5206.d:
υἱοθεσία, -ας, ἡ
 (cf. the cl. phrases, υἱὸν τίθεσθαι, θετὸς υἱός), frequently in Inscr. (see Deiss., BS, 239), adoption of a son (or daughter); metaphorically, of God's relation established 
  (a) with Israel: Rom.9:4; 
  (b) with Christ­ians: Rom.8:15, Gal.4:5, Eph.1:5; of its consummation, Rom.8:23.†
 (AS)

G5208.d:
ὕλη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Job.19:29 (†) Job.38:40 (סֻכָּה), Ps.69:2 B.l א (יָוֵן), Isa.10:17 (שָׁמִיר), Wis.11:17 15:13, Sir.28:10, 2Ma.2:24, 4Ma.1:29 * ;] 
  1. wood, forest, woodland (Thus., Xen., al.). 
  2. wood, timber, fuel (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.): Jas.3:5 (see Hort, Ja., 70, 104 f.). 
  3. = Lat. materia, esp. in Philosophy, matter (Arist. and later writers; Wis, ll. with).†

G5212.d:
ὑμέτερος, -α, -ον 
 poss. pron. of second of person(s) pl. (= emphasized genitive, ὑμῶν), 
 your, yours: John.7:6 8:17 15:20, Acts.27:34, Rom.11:31, 1 Cor.16:17, 2 Cor.8:8, Gal.6:13; as pred., Luke.6:20; τὸ ὑ., as subst., opposite to τ. ἀλλότριον, Luke.16:12 (WH, txt., R, mg., ἡμέτερον); objectively, ὑ. καύχησις, my glorying in you, 1 Cor.15:31.†

G5214.d:
ὑμνέω, -ῶ
 (ὕμνος) [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שִׁיר, יָדָה hi., etc. ;] 
  1. trans., with accusative of person(s) (in cl. also with accusative of thing(s)), to sing to, laud, sing to the praise of: Acts.16:25, Heb.2:12. 
  2. Intrans., to sing: in LXX and NT, of singing hymns and praises to God (Ps.65:13, al.), Matt.26:30, Mark.14:26 (see Swete, in l).†
 (AS)

G5217.d:
ὑπ-άγω 
 [in LXX: Exod.14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as seel., Tob.8:21, al. ;] 
a word of the vulgar language, in Pres. and imperfect only (Bl., § 53, 1). 
  I. Trans. 
  1. to lead or bring under, subdue (Hom., Hdt., al.; Ex, l.with). 
  2. to lead on slowly (Hdt., Xen., al.). 
  II. Intrans., to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart (so less frequently in cl.; Thuc., Eur., al.): absol., Matt.8:32 13:44, Mark.6:33, Luke.8:42 17:14, John.6:67 8:2 11:44 14:5, 28 18:8; οἱ ἐρχόμενοι κ. οἱ ὑπάγοντες, Mark.6:31; ὑπῆγον κ. ἐπίστευον, John.12:11; ἵνα ὑπαγῆτε κ. καρπὸν ψέρητε, John.15:16; opposite to ἔρχεσθαι, John.3:8 8:14; imperat., ὕπαγε, Matt.4:10 8:13 20:14, Mark.2:9 T, Mark.7:29 10:52; εἰς εἰρήνην (ἐν εἰ.), Mark.5:34, Jas.2:16; id. prefixed to another imperat. (Bl., § 79, 4), Matt.5:34 8:4 18:15 19:21 21:28 27:65 28:10, Mark.1:44 10:21 16:7, John.4:16 9:7, Rev.10:8; with καί inserted, Rev.16:1; euphemistically, of death, Matt.26:24, Mark.14:21; with adv.: ποῦ (which see), John.12:35 14:5 16:5, 1 John.2:11; ὅπου (which see), John.8:21-22 13:33, 36 14:4 Rev.14:4; ἐκεῖ, John.11:8; with prep.: πρός, John.7:33 13:3 16:5, 10 16:17; εἰς, Matt.9:6 20:4, 7, Mark.2:11 11:2 14:13, Luke.19:30, John.6:21 7:3 9:11 11:31, Rev.13:10 17:8, 11; εἰς . . . πρός, Matt.26:18, Mark.5:19; ἐπί, Luke.12:58; μετά, Matt.5:41; ὀπίσω, Matt.16:23, Mark.8:33; with inf., John.21:3.†
 (AS)

G5218.d:
ὑπακοή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (ὑπακούω), [in LXX: 2Ki.22:36 (עֲנָוָה); in Aq.: 2Ki.23:23 * ;] 
obedience (opposite to παρακοή); 
  1. in general, absol., εἰς ὑ., Rom.6:16; with genitive subjc., 2 Cor.7:15 10:6, Phm 21; with genitive obj., Rom.1:5 (Lft, Notes, 246) Rom.16:26, 1 Pet.1:22; τ. Χριστοῦ, 2 Cor.10:5. 
  2. Of obedience to God's commands: absol., 1 Pet.1:2; opposite to ἁμαρτία, Rom.6:16; τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, 1 Pet.1:14; with genitive subj., Rom.15:18 16:19. 
  3. Of Christ's obedience: absol., Heb.5:8; with genitive subj., Rom.5:19. 
 (The word is not found except in LXX, NT and eccl.).†
 (AS)

G5219.d:
ὑπακούω 
 [in LXX: chiefly for שָׁמַע ;] 
to listen, attend, hence, 
  (a) to answer a knock at a door (Plat., Xen., al.): Acts.12:13; 
  (b) to attend to, submit to, obey (Hdt., Thuc., al.): absol., Phil.2:12; with inf., Heb.11:8; with dative of person(s) (Plat., al.; but more frequently with genitive), Matt.8:27, Mark.1:27 4:41, Luke.8:25 17:6, Rom.6:16, Eph.6:1, 5, Col.3:20, 22, Heb.5:9, 1 Pet.3:6; with dative of thing(s), Acts.6:7, Rom.6:12 10:16, 2 Thess.1:8 3:14; before εἰς (by attraction, for dative; see ICC, in l), Rom.6:17.†
 (AS)

G5220.d:
ὕπανδρος, -ον 
 [in LXX: Num.5:20, 29 (אִישׁ תַּחַת), Pro.6:24, 29, Sir.9:9 41:21 * ;] 
under or subject to a man, married: γυνή, Rom.7:2 (Polyb., Diod., al.).†
 (AS)

G5222.d:
ὑπ-άντησις, -εως, ἡ
 (ὑπαντάω), [in LXX: Jdg.11:34, εἰς ὑ. (קִרְאָה), etc. ;] 
a going to meet: εἰς ὑ. (see M, Pro.14:1-35 n), Matt.8:34 25:1, John.12:13.†

G5223.d:
ὕπαρξις, -εως, ἡ
 (ὑπάρχω), [in LXX for רְכוּשׁ, הוֹן, etc. ;] 
  1. subsistence, existence (Arist., al.). 
  2. In late writers, = τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, substance, property: Heb.10:34; pl., Acts.2:45.†

G5224.d:
to have, possess; (n.) possessions; to be, exist 
to begin; to come into existence; to exist; to be, subsist, Actss 19:40; 28:18; to be in possession, to belong, Actss 3:6; 4:37; goods, possessions, property, Mt. 19:21; Lk. 8:3; to be, Lk. 7:25; 8:41

G5225.d:
ὑπάρχω 
 [in LXX for הָיָה, יֵשׁ, לוּן, etc.; τ. ὑπάρχοντα for מִקְנֶה, רְכוּשׁ, etc. ;] 
  1. to begin, make a beginning (Hom., Hdt., al.). 
  2. to be in existence, be ready, be at hand (Hdt., Thuc., al.): Acts.19:40 27:12, 21; before ἐν, Acts.28:18. 
  3. to be, prop, expressing continuance of an antecedent state or condition (cf. Gifford, Incarnation, 11 ff.; MM, xxv): with, nom, pred., Luke.8:41 9:48, Acts.4:34 7:55 8:16 16:3 19:36 21:20, 1 Cor.7:26 12:22, Jas.2:15, 2 Pet.3:11; ptcp. with pred., Luke.16:14 23:50, Acts.2:30, 32 17:24 22:3, Rom.4:19, 1 Cor.2:15, 2 Cor.8:17 12:16, Gal.1:14 2:14; pl., Luke.11:13, Acts.16:20, 37 17:29, 2 Pet.2:19; before ἐν, with dative of thing(s), Luke.7:25 16:23, Acts.5:4 10:12, 1 Cor.11:18, Phil.3:20; ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων (R, mg., being originally), Phil.2:6; ἐν, with dative of person(s), (among), 1 Cor.11:18; μακρὰν ἀπό, Acts.17:27; πρὸς τ. σωτηρίας, Acts.27:34. 
  4. to belong to (Thuc., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Acts.3:6 4:37 28:7, 2 Pet.1:8; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, one's belongings, possessions: with dative of person(s), Luke.8:3 12:15, Acts.4:32; with genitive of person(s), Matt.19:21 24:47 25:14, Luke.11:21 12:33, 44 14:33 16:1 19:8, 1 Cor.13:3, Heb.10:34 (cf. προ-υπάρχω).†

ὑπ-είκω

 (AS)

G5227.d:
ὑπ-εναντίος, -α, -ον 
 [in LXX for אָיַב, צַר, etc. ;] 
set over against, opposite. Metaphorical (Plat., Arist., al.), opposed to, contrary to: with dative of person(s), Col.2:14; absol., as subst., ὁ ὑ., Heb.10:27 (cf. Isa.26:11).†
 (AS)

G5228.d:
ὑπέρ (when following subst.—poët.—ὕπερ; so as adv., 2 Cor.11:23), 
 prep. with genitive, accusative  
  I. C. genitive, primarily of place (rest or motion), over, above, across, beyond, hence, metaphorically, 
  1. for, on behalf of: of prayer, Matt.5:44, Acts.8:24, Rom.10:1, Jas.5:16, al.; of laying down life, John.10:11, Rom.9:3, al.; esp. of Christ giving his life for man's redemption, Mark.14:24, John.10:15, Acts.21:13, Rom.5:6-8, al.; opposite to κατά, Mark.9:40, Luke.9:50, Rom.8:31. 
  2. Causal, for, because of, for the sake of: with genitive of person(s), Acts.5:41, Rom.1:5, Phil.1:29, 2 Cor.12:10, al.; with genitive of thing(s), John.11:4, Rom.15:8, 2 Cor.1:6, al. 
  3. = ἀντί (see M, Pr., 105), for, instead of, in the name of: 1 Cor.15:29, 2 Cor.5:15, 21 Gal.3:13, Col.1:7, Phm 13 (cf. Field, Notes, 225). 
  4. In more colourless sense, = περί (M, Pr., l.with), for, concerning, with regard to: Rom.9:27, 2 Cor.1:6 8:23 12:8, Phil.1:7, 2 Thess.2:1, al. 
  
  II. C. accusative, primarily of place, over, beyond, across, hence, metaphorically, of measure or degree in excess, above, beyond, over, more than: Matt.10:24, 37 Luke.6:40, Acts.26:13, 1 Cor.10:13, 2 Cor.1:8, Eph.1:22 3:20, Phm 16, al.; after comparatives = than (Jdg.11:25, al.), Luke.16:8, Heb.4:12. 
 
  III. As adv. (see supr. ad init.), more: ὕπερ ἐγώ, I more, 2 Cor.11:23; in compounds, see: ὑπεράνω, ὑπερλίαν, ὑπερπερισσῶς. 
 
  IV. In composition: over (ὑπεραίρω), beyond (ὑπερβάλλω), more (ὐπερνικάω), on behalf of (ὐπερεντυγχάνω).
 (AS)

G5229.d:
ὑπερ-αίρω

G5231.d:
ὑπερ-άνω 
 compound adv., [in LXX for עַל, מֵעָל, etc. ;] 
above: as prep. with genitive, Eph.1:21 4:10, Heb.9:5.†
 (AS)

G5232.d:
ὑπερ-αυξάνω 
 to increase beyond measure: 2 Thess.1:3 (see Lft., Notes, 98).†
 (AS)

G5233.d:
ὑπερ-βαίνω 
 [in LXX for עָבַר, etc. ;] 
  1. trans., to step over, trans­gress (R, overreach: 1 Thess.4:6). 
  2. Intrans., to transgress: metaphorically, 1 Thess.4:6 (R, txt.; see M, Th., in l).†
 (AS)

G5234.d:
ὑπερβαλλόντως 
 [in LXX: Job.15:11 א B (†) * ;] 
above measure: 2 Cor.11:23.†
 (AS)

G5235.d:
ὑπερ-βάλλω 
 [in LXX: Job.15:11 A (†), Sir.5:7 25:11, al. ;] 
  1. trans., to throw over or beyond. 
  2. Intrans., to run beyond. In both senses, metaphorically, to exceed, surpass, transcend: 2 Cor.3:10 9:14, Eph.1:19 2:7; with genitive obj., Eph.3:19.†
 (AS)

G5236.d:
ὑπερ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (ὑπερβάλλω), [in LXX: καθ᾽ ὑ., 4Ma.3:18 * ;] 
a throwing beyond. Metaphorical, excess, superiority, excellence: 2 Cor.4:7 12:7; καθ᾽ ὑπερβολήν, beyond measure, exceedingly, Rom.7:13, 1 Cor.12:31, 2 Cor.1:8, Gal.1:13; κ. ὑ. εἰς ὑ., beyond all measure, 2 Cor.4:17.†
 (AS)

G5237.d:
ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. 
 [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] 
to overlook: with accusative of thing(s), Acts.17:30 
 (AS)

G5238.d:
ὑπερ-έκεινα 
 comp. adv. (see Bl., 28, 2; M, Pr., 99), 
 beyond: as prep. with genitive, τὰ ὑ. ὑμῶν, 2 Cor.10:16 (Byz. and Ecc.1:1-18.).†
 (AS)

G5239.d:
ὑπερ-εκ-τείνω 
 to stretch out overmuch: metaphorically, ἑαυτούς, 2 Cor.10:14.† 
 (AS)

G5240.d:
ὑπερ-εκ-χύννω (Rec. -ύνω), late form of -χέω 
 to pour out over. Pass., to overflow, run over: Luke.6:38 (not elsewhere).†
 (AS)

G5241.d:
ὑπερ-εν-τυγχάνω 
 to intercede or make petition for (see Deiss., BS, 121 f.): before ὑπέρ, Rom.8:26.†
 (AS)

G5242.d:
ὑπερ-έχω 
 [in LXX: Gen.25:23 (אָמַץ), Exod.26:13 (עֲדַף), Sir.36:7, al. ;] 
  1. trans., to hold over or above. 
  2. Intrans. (when a noun follows, the case is governed by the prep.; see Bl., § 34, 1; 36, 8), to rise above, overtop; metaphorically, 
  (a) to be superior in rank, etc.: Rom.13:1, 1 Pet.2:13 (cf. Wis.6:6); 
  (b) to be superior, excel, surpass: with genitive (cl.; see supr.), Phil.2:3; with accusative (cl.; see supr.), Phil.4:7; as subst., τ. ὑπερέχον, the excel­lency, the surpassing worth, Phil.3:8.†
 (AS)

G5243.d:
ὑπερηφανία, -ας, ἡ
 (ὑπερήφανος, which see), [in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
haughtiness, arrogance, disdain: Mark.7:22 (Plat., Xen.).†
 (AS)

G5245.d:
ὑπερ-νικάω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Da TH Dan.6:3; in Sm.: Ps.43:1 * ;] 
to be more than conqueror: Rom.8:37 (eccl.).†
 (AS)

G5246.d:
ὑπέρ-ογκος, -ον 
 [in LXX: Deu.30:11 (פָּלָא), etc. ;] 
of excessive weight or size; metaphorically, excessive, immoderate, in late writers, of arrogant speech (see Mayor on Ju, l.with): n. pl., 2 Pet.2:18, Ju 16.†
 (AS)

G5247.d:
ὑπεροχή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (ὑπερέχω) [in LXX: Jer.52:22 (קוֹמָה), 2Ma.3:11, al. ;] 
a projection, eminence, as the peak of a mountain. Metaphorical (Arist.), excellence, pre-eminence: λόγου ἢ σοφίας, 1 Cor.2:1; οἱ ἐν ὑ (for a parallel to this phrase, see Deiss., BS, 255, and cf. 2Mac, l.with), 1 Tim.2:2.†
 (AS)

G5248.d:
ὑπερ-περισσεύω 
 to abound more exceedingly: Rom.5:21. Mid., in same sense (RV, overflow): with dative of thing(s), 2 Cor.7:4.†
 (AS)

G5249.d:
ὑπερ-περισσῶς 
 adv., 
beyond measure, exceedingly: Mark.7:37.†
 (AS)

G5250.d:
ὑπερ-πλεονάζω 
 to abound exceedingly: 1 Tim.1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).†
 (AS)

G5251.d:
ὑπερ-υψόω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Ps.37:35 (עָרִיץ) Ps.97:9 (עָלָה ni.), Da TH Dan.4:34 11:12 (רוּם), ib. LXX TH Dan.3:52 ff.* ;] 
  1. to exalt beyond measure, exalt to the highest place: Phil.2:9. 
  2. to extol (Da, ll. with).†
 (AS)

G5252.d:
ὑπερ-φρονέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 4Ma.13:1 4Mac 14:11 4Mac 16:2 * ;] 
  1. to be overproud, high-minded (Æsch.): μὴ ὑ. παρ᾽ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν (on the paranom., see Vau., in l), Rom.12:3. 
  2. to overlook, think slightly of (Thuc., Plat.).†
 (AS)

G5253.d:
ὑπερῷον, -ου, τό 
 (neut. of ὑπερῷος, above, ὑπέρ) [in LXX for עֲלִיָּה and cogn. forms ;] 
  1. in cl., the upper story or upper rooms where the women resided (Hom., a1.). 
  2. In LXX and NT, an upper chamber, roof-chamber, built on the flat roof of the house (see DB, iii, 674a): Acts.1:13 9:37, 39 20:8 (cf. 4Ki.23:22).†
 (AS)

G5254.d:
ὑπ-έχω 
 [in LXX: Ps.89:50 (נָשָׂא), La 5:7 (סָבַל), Wis.12:21, 2Ma.4:48 * ;] 
to hold or put under. Metaphorical, to undergo, suffer: δίκην, Ju 7 (Soph., Eur., al.).†
 (AS)

G5255.d:
ὑπήκοος, -ον
 (ὑπακσύω), [in LXX: John.17:13 (לָמַם) Pro.21:28 (שָׁמַע), etc. ;] 
giving ear, obedient, subject: Phil.2:8; with dative of person(s), Acts.7:39; εἰς πάντα, 2 Cor.2:9.†
 (AS)

G5256.d:
ὑπηρετέω, -ῶ
 (ὑπηρέτης) [in LXX: Wis.16:21, 24-25 19:6, Sir.39:4 * ;] 
prop., to serve as rower on a ship (Diod., al.). In cl. always metaphorically, to minister to, serve: with dative of person(s), Acts.13:36 20:34 24:23.†
 (AS)

G5257.d:
ὑπηρέτης, -ου, ὁ
 (ὑπό + ἐρέτης, a rower) [in LXX: Pro.14:35 (עֶבֶד), Wis.6:4, al. ;] 
prop., an under rower; hence, generally, a servant, attendant, minister: of a magistrate's attendant, Matt.5:25; of officers of the Synagogue or Sanhedrin, Matt.26:58, Mark.14:54, 65, Luke.4:20,  John.7:32, 45-46 18:3, 12 18:22 19:6, Acts.5:22, 26; of the attendants of kings, οἱ ὑ. οἱ ἑμοί John.18:36; of Christian ministers, Acts.13:5 26:16; ὑπηρέται λόγου, Luke.1:2; Χριστοῦ, 1 Cor.4:1; δοῦλοι κ. ὑ., John.18:18.†
 SYN.: see: διάκονος  (AS)

G5258.d:
ὕπνος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX for שֵׁנָה, חֲלוֹם, etc. ;] 
sleep: Matt.1:24, Luke.9:32, John.11:13, Acts.20:9; metaphorically, Rom.13:11.†
 (AS)

G5259.d:
ὑπό (before smooth breathing ὑπ᾽, Matt.8:9b, Luke.7:8b; before rough breathing ὑφ᾽, Rom.3:9; on the neglect of elision in Mt, Lk, ll. witha, Gal.3:22, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., iv), 
 prep. with genitive, dative (not in NT), accusative  
  I. C. genitive, primarily of place, under, hence, metaphorically, of the efficient cause, by: after passive verbs, with genitive of person(s), Matt.1:22, Mark.1:5, Luke.2:18, John.14:21, Acts.4:11, 1 Cor.1:11, Heb.3:4, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Matt.8:24, Luke.7:24, Rom.3:21, al.; with neut. verbs and verbs with pass, meaning, Matt.17:12, Mark.5:26, 1 Cor.10:9, 10 1 Thess.2:14, al. 
  II. C. accusative, under; 
  1. of motion: Matt.5:15 8:8, Mark.4:21, Luke.13:34; hence, metaphorically, of subjection, Rom.7:14, 1 Cor.15:27, Gal.3:22, 1 Pet.5:6, al. 
  2. Of position: John.1:49, Acts.4:12, Rom.3:13, 1 Cor.10:1, al.; hence, metaphorically, under, subject to, Matt.8:9, Rom.3:9, 1 Cor.9:20, Gal.4:5, al. 
  3. Of time, about: Acts.5:21. 
  III. In composition: under (ὑποδέω), hence, of subjection (ὑποτάσσω), compliance (ὑπακούω), secrecy (ὑποβάλλω), diminution (ὑποπνέω). 
 (AS)

G5260.d:
ὑπο-βάλλω 
 [in LXX: ??Dan.3:9 A, I Est.2:18 * ;] 
to throw or put under. Metaphorical, 
  (a) to subject, submit; 
  (b) to suggest, whisper, prompt; 
  (with) to suborn (see Field, Notes, 113), instigate: with accusative of person(s), Acts.6:11.†
 (AS)

G5261.d:
ὑπογραμμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (ὑπογράφω, (a) to write under; (b) to trace letters for copying), [in LXX: 2Ma.2:28 * ;] 
  1. a writing-copy, hence, 
  2. an example: 1 Pet.2:11 (Philo).†
 (AS)

G5262.d:
ὑπό-δειγμα, -τος, τό
 (ὑποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: Eze.42:15, Sir.44:16, 2Ma.6:28 2Mac 6:31, 4Ma.17:23 * ;] 
used by later writers (Xen. onwards) for παράδειγμα (see Rutherford, NPhr., 62), 
  (a) a figure, copy: Heb.8:5 9:23; 
  (b) an example: for imitation, John.13:15, Jas.5:10; for warning, Heb.4:11, 2 Pet.2:6.†
 SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑποτύπωσις (see DB, iii. 696b)  (AS)

G5263.d:
ὑπο-δείκνυμι 
 [in LXX for נָגַד hi., etc. ;] 
  1. to show secretly. 
  2. to show by tracing out; hence, generally, to teach, make known: with dative of person(s), Luke.6:47 12:5, Acts.9:16; id. with inf., Matt.3:7, Luke.3:7; before, ὅτι, Acts.20:35.†
 (AS)

G5264.d:
ὑπο-δέχομαι 
 [in LXX: Tob.7:8-9 Jdth.13:13 A, 1Ma.16:15, 4Ma.13:17 * ;] 
to receive under one's roof, receive as a guest, entertain hospitably: with accusative of person(s), Luke.19:6, Acts.17:7, Jas.2:25; εἰς τ. οἶκον, Luke.10:38 (see MM, xxv).†
 (AS)

G5266.d:
ὑπόδημα, -τος, τό
 (ὑποδέω), [in LXX for נָעַל ;] 
a sole bound under the foot, a sandal: Matt.3:11 10:10, Mark.1:7, Luke.3:16 10:4 15:22 22:35, John.1:27; τ. ποδῶν, Acts.7:33 (LXX) Acts.13:25.†
 SYN.: σανδάλιον, q.v  (AS)

G5267.d:
ὑπόδικος, -ον 
 brought to trial, answerable to: with dative of person(s), τ. θεῷ, Rom.3:19 (see MM, xxv).†
 (AS)

G5268.d:
ὑπο-ζύγιος, -α, -ον 
 [in LXX for חֲמוֹר ;] 
under the yoke; as subst., τ . (Hdt., al.), a beast of burden; colloq., an ass (see Deiss., BS, 160 f.), and so always in LXX and NT: Matt.21:5 (LXX), 2 Pet.2:16.†
 (AS)

G5269.d:
ὑπο-ζώννυμι 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.3:19 * ;] 
to undergird (Hdt., al.; ὑπὸ τ. μάστους, 2Mac, l.with); of a ship, to undergird or frap: Acts.27:17 (see DB, ext. 367a).†
 (AS)

G5270.d:
ύπο-κάτω  comp. adv. (see M, Pr., 99), 
 [in LXX chiefly for תַּחַת ;] 
below, under: as prep. with genitive, Matt.22:44, Mark.6:11 7:28 12:36 (Rec., R, txt., ὑποπόδιον, as in LXX), Luke.8:16, John.1:51, Heb.2:8" (LXX), Rev.5:3, 13 6:9 12:1.†
 (AS)

G5271.d:
ὑπο-κρίνομαι 
 [in LXX: (Job.40:2) אּ1 (AB אּ2 ἀπο-, עָנָה), Sir.1:29 35:15 (32:15) Sir.36:2 (33:2), 2Ma.5:25 2Mac 6:21 2Mac 6:24, 4Ma.6:15 4Mac 6:17 * ;] 
  1. = Att.. ἀποκρίνομαι (which see), to answer, reply (Hom., Hdt., al.). 
  2. to answer on the stage, play apart (Arist., al.). Metaphorical, to feign, pretend (Demos., Polyb.): with accusative and inf., Luke.20:20 (cf. Ps sol 4:22).†
 (AS)

G5272.d:
ὑπό-κρισις, -εως, ἡ
 (ὑποκρίνομαι, which see) [in LXX: 2Ma.6:25 * ;] 
  1. a reply, answer (Hdt.). 
  2. play-acting (Arist., Polyb., al.). Metaphorical, pretence, hypocrisy: Matt.23:28, Mark.12:15, Luke.12:1, Gal.2:13, 1 Tim.4:2, 1 Pet.2:1 (Polyb., Pss Sng.4:7).†
 (AS)

G5273.d:
ὑπο-κριτής, -οῦ, ὁ
 (ὑποκρίνομαι, which see) [in LXX Job.34:30 36:13 (חָנֵף) * ;] 
  1. one who answers, an interpreter (Plat.). 
  2. a stage player, actor (Plut., Xen., al.). Metaphorical (in LXX and NT), a pretender, dissembler, hypocrite: Matt.6:2, 5 6:16 7:5 15:7 22:18 23:13-15 24:51, Mark.7:6 Luke.6:42 12:56 13:15.†
 (AS)

G5274.d:
ὑπο-λαμβάνω 
 [in LXX: Job.2:4 4:1 and frequently (עָנָה), Ps.48:9 (דָּמָה pi.), Tob.6:17, Wis.17:2, 3Ma.3:8 3Mac 3:11, al. ;] 
  1. to take or bear up (by supporting from beneath): with accusative of person(s), Acts.1:9. 
  2. to receive, welcome, entertain (Xen.): III Jn 8. 
  3. to catch up in speech (Hdt., al.; Jb, ll. with): Luke.10:30. 
  4. Of mental action, to assume, suppose (Xen., al.; To, Wis, 3Mac, ll. with): Acts.2:15; before ὅτι (see Bl., § 70, 2), Luke.7:43.†
 (AS)

G5275.d:
ὑπο-λείπω 
 [in LXX chiefly (pass.) for יָתַר ni., שָׁאַר ni. ;] 
to leave remaining (Hom., Thuc., al.): pass., of survivors, Rom.11:3.†
 (AS)

G5276.d:
ὑπολήνιον, -ου, τό
 (ὑπό, ληνός), [in LXX: Jol.3:13 (4:13), Hag.2:17, (16), Zec.14:10, Isa.16:10 (יֶקֶב) * ;] 
a vessel or trough beneath a winepress to  receive the juice (RV, a pit for the winepress): Mark.12:1 (see Swete, in l, and cf. ληνός).†
 (AS)

G5277.d:
ὑπο-λιμτάνω 
 collat. form of ὑπολείπω, 
 to leave behind: 1 Pet.2:21.†
 (AS)

G5278.d:
ὑπο-μένω 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָוָה, also for יָחַל hi., etc. ;] 
  1. in-trans., to stay behind: before ἐν, Luke.2:43; ἐκεῖ, Acts.17:14. 
  2. Trans., 
  (a) with accusative, to await, wait for: Rom.8:24 (Hom., Hdt., Xen., al.); 
  (b) of things, to bear patiently, endure: absol., Matt.10:22 24:13, Mark.13:13, 2 Tim.2:12, Jas.5:11, 1 Pet.2:20; τ. θλίψει (dative of circumstance), Rom.12:12; before εἰς, Heb.12:7; with accusative of thing(s), 1 Cor.13:7, 2 Tim.2:10, Heb.10:32 12:2-3, Jas.1:12.†
 SYN.: μακροθυμέω (see: ὑπομονή)  (AS)

G5279.d:
ὑπο-μιμνήσκω 
 [in LXX: 3Ki.4:3 B ( hi.), Wis.12:1 18:22, 4Ma.18:14 * ;] 
to cause one to remember, put one in mind or remind one of: with accusative of thing(s), 2 Tim.2:14, 3 John.10; with dupl. accusative (Thus., al.), John.14:26; with accusative of person(s), before περί, 2 Pet.1:12; id., before ὅτι, Ju 5; with inf., Titus.3:1; pass., with genitive of thing(s), Luke.22:61.†
 (AS)

G5280.d:
ὑπόμινησις, -εως, ἡ
 (ὑπομιμνήσκω) [in LXX: Ps.71:6 א (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.16:11, 2Ma.6:17 * ;] 
a reminding, reminder: ἐν ὑ., 2 Pet.1:13 3:1; with genitive, 2 Tim.1:5.†
 (AS)

G5281.d:
ὑπο-μονή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (ὑπομένω) [in LXX for מִקְוֶה and cogn. forms; frequently in 4Mac ;] 
  1. a remaining behind (Arist.). 
  2. patient enduring, endurance: Luke.8:15 21:19, Rom.5:3-4 15:4-5, 2 Cor.6:4 12:12, Col.1:11, 2 Thess.1:4, 1 Tim.6:11, 2 Tim.3:10, Titus.2:2, Heb.10:36, Jas.1:3-4 5:11, 2 Pet.1:6, Rev.2:2-3, 19 13:10 14:12; δι᾽ ὑπομονῆς, Rom.8:25, Heb.12:1; with genitive of person(s), 2 Thess.3:5 (ICC, in l), Rev.3:10; with genitive of thing(s), Rom.2:7, 2 Cor.1:6, 1 Thess.1:3; before ἐν, Rev.1:9.†
 SYN.: see: μακροθυμία, and cf. Hort on Jas.1:3  (AS)

G5282.d:
ὑπο νοέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Da TH Dan.7:25 (סְבַר), Tob.8:16, Jdth.14:14, Sir.23:21 * ;] 
to suspect, conjecture: Acts.25:18; with accusative and inf., Acts.13:25 27:27.† 
 (AS)

G5283.d:
ὑπόνοια, -ας, ἡ
 (ὑπονοέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 4:16, 32 5:6 (רַעְיוֹן), Sir 3:34* ;] 
a suspicion: 1 Tim.6:4.†
 (AS)

G5284.d:
ὑπο-πλέω 
 to sail under, i.e. under the lee of: with accusative, Acts.27:4, 7.†
 (AS)

G5285.d:
ὑπο-πνέω 
  1. to blow underneath (Arist.). 
  2. to blow gently: Acts.27:13.†
 (AS)

G5286.d:
ὑποπόδιον, -ου, τό
 (ὑπό, πούς), [in LXX: Ps.99:5 110:1, Isa.66:1, La 2:1 (הֲדֹם) * ;] 
a footstool (= cl. θρᾶνος): Jas.2:3; metaphorically, Matt.5:35, Mark.12:36 (ὑποκάτω, WH, R, mg.), Luke.20:43, Acts.2:35 7:49, Heb.1:13 10:13 (all, except Mt, l.with, from LXX, Ps.110:1, Isa.66:1) (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 223).†
 (AS)

G5287.d:
ὑπό-στασις, -εως, ἡ
 (ὑφίστημι, to set under, stand under, support) [in LXX for מַצָּב (1Ki.13:23 14:4 B), תִּקְוָה (Rut.1:12, Eze.19:5), etc., also in Wis.16:21 ;] 
  1. a support, base or foundation (in various senses). 
  2. substance (Arist., al.; opposite to φαντασία, ἔμφασις): Heb.1:3 
  3. steadiness,  firmness (Polyb., al.), hence, assurance, confidence: 2 Cor.9:4 11:17, Heb.3:14 11:1 (here perhaps title-deed, as that which gives reality or guarantee; see MM, xxv).†
 (AS)

G5288.d:
ὑπο-στέλλω 
 [in LXX: Deu.1:17 (גּוּר), Job.13:8 (נָשָׂא פָּנִים), Hab.2:4 (עָפַל pu.), Hag.1:10 (כָּלָא), Exod.23:21, Wis.6:7, 3Ma.5:28 * ;] 
  1. to draw in, let down (ἱστίον, οὐράν, etc.). 
  2. to draw back, withdraw: ἑαυτόν, Gal.2:12 (Polyb., al.; see Lft., in l). Mid., to shrink or draw back: Heb.10:38 (LXX); before τοῦ, with inf., Acts.20:27; οὐδέν, Acts.20:20.†
 (AS)

G5289.d:
ὑπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (ὑποστέλλω), 
  1. a letting down, lowering (Plut.). 
  2. a shrinking back (Hesych.): οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς (on the genitive, see Bl., § 35, 2), Heb.10:39.†
 (AS)

G5290.d:
ὑπο-στρέφω 
 [in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ], 
  1. trans., to turn back or about (Hem.). 
  2. Intrans., to turn back, return: Luke.2:20, 43 8:37, 40 9:10 10:17 17:15 19:12 23:48, 56, Acts.8:28; with inf., Luke.17:18; before διά, Acts.20:3; εἰς, Luke.1:56 2:45 4:14 7:10 8:3 9:8 11:24 24:33, 52, Acts.1:12 8:25 13:13, 34 14:21 21:6 22:17 23:32, Gal.1:17; ἀπό, Luke.4:1 24:9, Heb.7:1; ἐκ, Acts.12:25, 2 Pet.2:21.†
 (AS)

G5291.d:
ὑπο-στρωννύω 
 [in LXX: Isa.58:5 (יָצָא hi.), etc. ;] 
late form of ὑπο-στορέννυμι, to spread or strew under: with accusative of thing(s), Luke.19:36.†
 (AS)

G5292.d:
ὑπο-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Wis.18:16 A * ;] 
subjection: 2 Cor.9:13, Gal.2:5. 1 Tim.2:11 3:4.†
 (AS)

G5293.d:
ὑπο-τάσσω 
 [in LXX for דָבַר hi., דָּמַם, שׂוּם, שִׁית, etc. ;] 
  1. as a military term, to place or rank under (Polyb.). 
  2. to subject, put in subjection: 1 Cor.15:27, Phil.3:21, Heb.2:5, 8; pass., Rom.8:20, 1 Cor.15:27-28, 1 Pet.3:22, Eph.1:22.  [in LXX: Jdg.20:37 B (-), Sir.13:9, 2Ma.12:12 * ;]

to strike under the eye, give a black eye:

swine: fem. (sow), 2 Pet.2:22,†

ὕσσωπος, -ου, ἡ 
 [in LXX for אֵזוֹב ;]

 (ὕστερος), [in LXX for חָסֵר, חָדַל etc. ;]

  (b) with genitive of person(s), to come short of, be inferior to: 2 Cor.11:5; οὐδέν (in nothing, in no respect), 2 Cor.12:11;

G5303.d:
ὑστέρημα, -τος, τό
 (ὑστερέω), [in LXX: Jdg.18:10 19:19-20, Ps.34:9 (מַחְסוֹר), Ecc.1:15 (חֶסְרוֹן), Est.6:9 (ὑ. εἶναι, חֲשַׁח) * ;]

murder, slaughter: Mark.15:7, Luke.23:19, 25, Acts.9:1, Rom.1:29; φ. μαχαίρης (cf. Exod.17:13, al.), Heb.11:37; pl., Matt.15:19, Mark.7:21, Rev.9:21.†
 (AS)

G5409.d:
φορέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Pro.16:23 (יָסַף hi.), Sir.11:5, al. ;] 
frequent. of φέρω, denoting repeated or habitual action (cf. Tr., Syn., § lviii), most commonly used of clothing, weapons, etc., to bear constantly, wear: Matt.11:8, John.19:5, Rom.13:4, 1 Cor.15:49, Jas.2:3.†
 (AS)

G5410.d:
φόρον, -ου, τό
 (Lat. forum): Ἀππίου Φ., see: Ἄππιος 
 (AS)

G5411.d:
φόρος, .-ου, ὁ
 (φέρω), [in LXX chiefly for מַס, also for מִדָּה,  etc. ;] 
tribute paid by a subject nation (cf. 1Ma.10:33): φ. δοῦναι (1Ma.8:4 1Mac 8:7), Luke.20:22 23:2; ἀποδοῦναι, Rom.13:7; τελεῖν, Rom.13:6 (Hdt., al.).†
 SYN.: κῆνσος, τέλος (which see)  (AS)

G5412.d:
φορτίζω
 (φόρτος), [in LXX: Eze.16:33 (שָׁחַד) * ;] 
to load: with dupl. accusative, Luke.11:46; pass., to be laden: metaphorically (EV, heavy laden), Matt.11:28.†
 (AS)

G5413.d:
φορτίον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of φόρτος), [in LXX chiefly for מַשָּׂא ;] 
a burden, load: of the cargo of a ship (Hdt., al.), Acts.27:10; metaphorically, Matt.11:30 23:4, Luke.11:46, Gal.6:5.†
 SYN.: βάρος (which see), ὄγκος  (AS)

G5414.d:
φόρτος, -ου, ὁ
 (φέρω), 
a load: esp. of a ship's cargo (Hom., Hdt., and late prose writers), Acts.27:10, Rec.†
 (AS)

G5415.d:
φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, see Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ 
 (Lat.) Fortunatus: 1 Cor.16:17 (see Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).†
 (AS)

G5416.d:
φραγέλλιον, -ου, τό
 (Lat. flagellum), a scourge: John.2:15.†
 (AS)

G5417.d:
φραγελλόω, -ῶ
 (φραγέλλιον, which see), 
to scourge: with accusative, Matt.27:26, Mark.15:15 (eccl.).†
 (AS)

G5418.d:
φραγμός, -oῦ, ὁ
 (φράσσω), [in LXX chiefly for גָּדֵר, גְּדֵרָה, also for גְּדֵרָה, etc. ;] 
  1. prop., a fencing in (Soph., OT, 1387). 
  2. = φράγμα, a fence: Matt.21:33, Mark.12:1, Luke.14:23. Metaphorical, μεσότοιχον (which see) τοῦ φ., genitive epexeg., Eph.2:14 (see Ellic., in l).†
 (AS)

G5419.d:
φράζω 
 [in LXX: Job.6:24 (בִּין hi.) Job.12:8 (יָרָה hi.), Dan LXX 2:4 (חָוָה pa.) * ;] 
to show forth, tell, declare, explain: Matt.13:36 (WH, RV, διασάφησον) Matt.15:15.†
 (AS)

G5420.d:
φράσσω 
 [in LXX: Job.38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Hos.2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pro.21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;] 
to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, Heb.11:33; στόμα, metaphorically, Rom.3:19; pass., καύχησις, 2 Cor.11:10.†
 (AS)

G5421.d:
φρέαρ, -ατος, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for בְּאֵר ;] 
a well: Luke.14:5, Sng.4:11-12; φ. τῆς ἀβύσσου, Rev.9:1-2.†
 (AS)

G5422.d:
φρεν-απατάω, -ῶ
 (φρεναπάτης), 
to deceive one's mind (Lft., deceive by fancies, see Ga., l.with): with accusative of person(s), Gal.6:3.†
 (AS)

G5423.d:
φρεναπάτης, -ου, ὁ
 (φρήν, ἀπάτη), 
a deceiver (B1., deceiver of his own mind, § 28, 5.2, where see ref. to π.): Titus.1:10 (eccl.).†
 (AS)

G5424.d:
φρήν  genitive, φρενός, ἡ, 
 [in LXX most frequently in Pr (Pro.6:32, al.) and chiefly for לֵב; also 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:47 ;] 
chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., al., both sing. and pl.; 
  1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff. 
  2. heart, mind, thought: pl., 1 Cor.14:20 (see Edwards, Eng.-Gr. Lex., App., 1).†
 (AS)

G5425.d:
φρίσσω
 (Att.. -ττω, and so 4Ma.14:9 4Mac 17:7) [in LXX: Job.4:15 ( pi.), etc. ;] 
  1. to be rough, bristle. 
  2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Jas.2:19 (see Hort, in l).†
 (AS)

G5426.d:
φρονέω, -ῶ
 (φρήν), [in LXX: Deu.32:29, Zec.9:2 (חָכָם), Ps.94:8 (שָׂכַל hi.), Isa.44:18 (בִּין) Isa.44:28, Est.8:13, Wis.1:1 14:30, 1Ma.10:20, 2Ma.9:12;  2Ma.14:8 2Mac 14:26 * ;] 
  1. to have understanding (Hon., al.). 
  2. to think, to be minded in a certain way: ὡς νήπιος, 1 Cor.13:11; with accusative (usually neut., adj., or pron., as frequently in cl.), ὃ δεῖ, Rom.12:3; ἃ, Acts.28:22; τοῦτο, Phil.3:15; τι ἑτέρως, ib.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο, Gal.5:10; τ. αὐτὸ φ. (Deiss., BS, 256), to be of the same mind, 2 Cor.13:11, Phil.2:2 4:2; id. before εἰς (ἐν) ἀλλήλους(οις), Rom.12:16 15:5; τ. ἓν φ., Phil.2:2 (Lft., in l); before ὑπέρ, Phil.1:7. 
  3. to have in mind, be mindful of, think of (Hdt., Xen., al.; Es, 1Mac, ll. with): τὰ τ. θεοῦ, opposite to τ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Matt.16:23, Mark.8:33; τὰ τ. σαρκός, opposite to τ. τ. πνεύρατος, Rom.8:5; τ. ἐπίγεια, Phil.3:19; τὰ ἄνω, opposite to τ. ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, Col.3:2; τοῦτο φρονεῖτε (RV, have this mind in you), Phil.2:5; ὑψηλά, Rom.12:16; φ. ἡμέραν (to observe a day), Rom.14:6; before ὑπέρ, Phil.4:10 (cf. κατα-, παρα-, περι-, ὑπερ-φρσνέω).†
 (AS)

G5427.d:
φρόνημα, -τος, τό
 (φρονέω), [in LXX: 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 13:9 * ;] 
that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 88), the thought: Rom.8:6-7, 27.†
 (AS)

G5428.d:
φρόνησις, -εως, ἡ
 (φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּינָה, תָּבוּן, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;] 
understanding, practical wisdom, prudence: Luke.1:17, Eph.1:8.†
 SYN.: see: σοφία, and cf. Lft., Notes, 317  (AS)

G5429.d:
φρόνιμος, -ον
 (φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם etc. ;] 
practically wise, sensible, prudent: Matt.10:16 24:45, Luke.12:42, 1 Cor.10:15; opposite to μωρός, Matt.7:24 25:2, 4 25:8-9, 1 Cor.4:10; to ἄφρων, 2 Cor.11:19; φ. παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ (EV, wise in one's own conceit), Rom.11:25 12:16 (cf. Pro.3:7); compar., -ώτερος, Luke.16:8.†
 SYN.: see: σοψός  (AS)

G5431.d:
φροντίζω
 (φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: 1Ki.9:5 (דָּאַג), Ps.40:17 (חָשַׁב), al. ;] 
to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., with accusative, with genitive), with inf., Titus.3:8 (see Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 206 f.).†
 (AS)

G5432.d:
φρουρέω, -ῶ 
 (φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Est.4:56, Jdth.3:6, Wis.17:16, 1Ma.11:3 * ;] 
to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: 2 Cor.11:32; metaphorically, Gal.3:23, Phil.4:7, 1 Pet.1:5.†
 (AS)

G5433.d:
φρυάσσω
 (so Ps, l.with, NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Ps.2:1 (רָגַשׁ), 2Ma.7:34 R, 3Ma.2:2 * ;] 
prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaphorical, to be wanton, insolent: Acts.4:25 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G5434.d:
φρύγανον, -ου, τό
 (φρύγω, to parch), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, also for חָרוּל, etc. ;] 
a dry stick: pl., brushwood: Acts.28:3.†
 (AS)

G5435.d:
φρυγία, -ας, ἡ
 (prop., the adj., Φρυγίος, -α, -ον; sc. γῆ, χώρα), 
Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor: Acts.2:10; Φ. καὶ Γαλατικὴ χώρα (Γ. χ. κ. Φ.), Acts.16:6 18:23 (on these phrases see DB, i, 89 f.; CGT, Gal., xxii f.).†
 (AS)

G5437.d:
φυγή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (φεύγω), [in LXX chiefly for מָנוֹס and cogn. forms ;] 
flight: Matt.24:20.†
 (AS)

G5439.d:
φυλακίζω 
 [in LXX: Wis.18:4 * ;] 
to imprison: Acts.22:19.†
 (AS)

G5440.d:
φυλακτήριον, -ου, τό 
  1. an outpost, fortification (Thuc., al.). 
  2. a safeguard (Plat.). 
  3. an amulet (Plut., al.); in NT for the Talmudic תְּפִלִּין, a prayer fillet, a phylactery, a small strip of parchment on which portions of the law were written and worn on the forehead and next the heart (cf. Exod.13:16): Matt.23:5.†
 (AS)

G5441.d:
φύλαξ, -ακος, ὁ
 (φυλάσσω), [in LXX for שָׁמַר, צוּר ;] 
a guard, keeper: Acts.5:23 12:6, 19.†
 (AS)

G5443.d:
φυλή, ῆς, ἡ
 [in LXX chiefly for; מַטֶּה, also for שֵׁבֶט, מִשְׁפָּחָה, etc. ;] 
a body of men united by kinship or habitation, a clan or tribe: of the tribes of Israel, Matt.19:28, Luke.2:36 22:30, Acts.13:21, Rom.11:1, Phil.3:5, Heb.7:13-14, Jas.1:1, Rev.5:5 7:4-8 21:12; of the tribes of the earth, the peoples and nations, Matt.24:30, Rev.1:7 5:9 7:9 11:9 13:7 14:6.†
 (AS)

G5444.d:
φύλλον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for עָלֶה ;] 
a leaf: Matt.21:19 24:32, Mark.11:13 13:28, Rev.22:2.†
 (AS)

G5445.d:
φύραμα, -τος, τό
 (φυράω, to mix), [in LXX: Exod.8:3 (Exod.7:28) Exod.12:34 (מִשְׁאֶרֶת), מִשְׁאֶרֶת), Num.15:20-21 (עֲרִיסָה) * ;] 
that which is mixed or kneaded, a lump: of dough, Rom.11:16, 1 Cor.5:6-7, Gal.5:9; of clay, Rom.9:21.†
 (AS)

G5446.d:
φυσικός, -ή, -όν 
 (ψύσις), 
natural 
  (a) produced by nature, innate (Xen., Arist., al.); 
  (b) according to nature (Arist., Diod., al.): opposite to παρὰ φύσιν, Rom.1:26-27; 
  (with) governed by mere natural instinct (of. Plut., Mor., 706 A): ζῷα γεγεννημένα φ. (RV, born mere animals; Mayor, born creatures of instinct; ICC, animals born of mere nature), 2 Pet.2:12,†
 (AS)

G5447.d:
φυσικῶς 
 adv., 
naturally, by nature: Ju 10.†
 (AS)

G5448.d:
φυσιόω, -ῶ
 (φῦσα, bellows), = cl. φυσάω, 
to puff or blow up, inflate. Metaphorical, to puff up, make proud: 1 Cor.8:1. Pass., to be puffed up with pride: 1 Cor.4:18-19 5:2 13:4; before ὑπό, Col.2:18; before ὑπὲρ . . . κατά, 1 Cor.4:6 (on the form of the subjc., see M, Pr., 54; Bl., § 22, 3).†
 (AS)

G5450.d:
φυσίωσις, -εως, ἡ
 (φυσιόω), 
a puffing up, swelling with pride: pl., 2 Cor.12:20.†
 (AS)

G5451.d:
φυτεία, -ας, ἡ
 (φυτεύω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (נָטַע), Mic.1:6, Eze.17:7 (מַטָּע) * ;] 
  1. a planting (Xen., al.; LXX). 
  2. = φύτευμα, that which is planted, a plant (Inscr.): Matt.15:13.†
 (AS)

G5452.d:
φυτεύω
 (φυτόν, a plant, φύω), [in LXX chiefly for נָטַע, also for שָׁתַל, etc. ;] 
to plant: Luke.17:28, 1 Cor.3:6-8; with accusative, φυτείαν, Matt.15:13; ἀμπελῶνα, Matt.21:33, Mark.12:1, Luke.20:9, 1 Cor.9:7; pass., before ἐν, Luke.13:6 17:6.†
 (AS)

G5453.d:
φύω
 [in LXX: Pro.26:9, Eze.37:8 (עָלָה), etc. ;] 
  1. trans., to bring forth, produce (of men, to beget); pass., to spring up, grow: Luke.8:6, 8. 
  2. Intrans., in 2 aor., pf., plpf., and rarely in present (see LS, see word, A, II.), to spring up: Heb.12:15.†
 (AS)

G5454.d:
φωλεός, -οῦ ὁ 
 a hole, den, lair: Matt.8:20, Luke.9:58.†
 (AS)

G5455.d:
φωνέω, -ῶ 
 (φωνή), [in LXX for קָרָא (Jer.17:11, al.), etc. ;] 
  I. Intrans. 
  1. Of persons, to call out, cry out, speak aloud: Luke.8:8; φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, Mark.1:26, Acts.16:28; ἐφώνησε (φωνῇ μεγάλῇ) λέγων, Luke.8:54, Rev.14:18; φωνήσαντες ἐπύθοντο, Acts.10:18. 
  2. Of the cries of animals (rarely in cl.; Isa.38:14, Je, l.with): of a cock, to crow, Matt.26:34, Mark.14:30, Luke.22:3, John.13:38 18:27. 
  II. Trans. (in cl. chiefly poët.), with accusative of person(s), to call, summon, invite: Matt.20:32 27:47, Mark.9:35 10:49 15:35, Luke.14:12 16:2 19:15, John.1:49 2:9 4:16 10:3 11:28 12:17 18:33, Acts.9:41 10:7; to address, call by name (Soph.), John.13:13 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπι-, προσ-, συν-φωνέω).†
 (AS)

G5458.d:
φωστήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
 (φῶς), [in LXX: Gen.1:14, 16 (מָאוֹר), Dan LXX 12:3 (זֹהַר), I Est.8:79, Wis.13:2, Sir.43:7 * ;] 
a luminary, light: Phil.2:15, Rev.21:11.†
 SYN.: φέγγος, φῶς  (AS)

G5459.d:
φωσ-φόρος, -ον
 (φῶς, φέρω), 
light-bringing; as subst., ὁ φ., the morning star (Plat., al.; cf. ἐωσφόρος, Isa.14:12, Job.3:9, Ps.110:3): metaphorically, 2 Pet.1:19 (see Mayor, in l).†
 (AS)

G5460.d:
φωτεινός (WH, φωτινός), ή, όν
 (φῶς), [in LXX: Sir.17:31 23:19 * ;] 
bright, light: νεφέλη, Matt.17:5; opposite to σκοτεινός, Matt.6:22, Luke.11:34, 36.†
 (AS)

G5461.d:
φωτίζω
 (φῶς) [in LXX for אוֹר hi, יָרָה hi., etc. ;] 
  1. intrans., to shine, give light (Arist., Plut., a1.): before ἐπί, Rev.22:5. 
  2. Trans. 
  (a) to illumine, enlighten (Diod., Plut., al.): with accusative, Luke.11:36, Rev.21:23; pass., Rev.18:1. Metaphorical, of spiritual enlightenment (Ps.119:130, Sir.45:17, al.): John.1:9, Eph.1:18 3:9, R, txt., Heb.6:4 10:32; 
  (b) to bring to light, make known (Polyb.): 1 Cor.4:5, Eph.3:9, R, mg., 2 Tim.1:10 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 107 f.).†
 (AS)

G5462.d:
φωτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (φωτίζω) [in LXX: Job.3:9, Ps.27:1 44:3 78:14 139:11 (אוֹר), Ps.89:8 (מָאוֹר) * ;] 
illumination, light: metaphorically, 1 Cor.4:4 4:6.†
 (AS)

G5463.d:
χαίρω 
 [in LXX for שָׂמַח (Gen.45:16, al.), גִּיל (Pro.2:14, al.), etc.; inf., as greeting (see infr.), Isa.48:22 57:21 שָׁלוֹם), 1Ma.10:18, 2Ma.1:1 and frequently in these books ;] 
  1. to rejoice, be glad: Mark.14:11, Luke.15:5, 32 19:6, 37 22:5 23:8, John.8:56 20:20, Acts.5:41 8:39 11:23 13:48, 2 Cor.6:10 7:7 13:9, Phil.2:17, 28,  Col.2:5, 1 Thess.5:16, 1 Pet.4:13, 3 John.3; χ. καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι, Matt.5:12; κ. σκιρτᾶν, Luke.6:23; opposite to κλαίειν, Rom.12:15, 1 Cor.7:30; to κλαίειν κ. θρηνεῖν John.16:20; to λύπην ἔχειν, John.16:22; with cogn. accusative, χ. χαρὰν μεγάλην, Matt.2:10; χαρᾷ χ. (B1., § 38, 3; Dalman, Words, 34 f.), John.3:29; ἡ χαρὰ ᾗ χαίρομεν, 1 Thess.3:9; with prep. (Bl., 38, 2), ἐπί, with dative (simple dative in cl.), Matt.18:13, Luke.1:14 13:17, Acts.15:31, Rom.16:19, 1 Cor.13:6 16:17, 2 Cor.7:13, Rev.11:10; διά, John.3:29 11:15, 1 Thess.3:9; ἐν, Phil.1:18; ἀπό, 2 Cor.2:3; with accusative (Dem.), Phil.2:18; before ὅτι, John.14:28, 2 Cor.7:9 7:16, 2 John.4; ἐν τούτῳ ὅτι, Luke.10:20; with dative, Rom.12:1; ἐν κυρίῳ, Phil.4:10 
  2. In salutations, imperat., χαῖρε, χαίρετε, 
  (a) at meeting, hail: Matt.26:49 27:29, Mark.15:18, Luke.1:28, John.19:3; pl., Matt.28:9; so χχαίρειν λέγω, to give greeting, II Jn 11; in letters, χαίρειν (sc. λέγει; 81, 1), greeting: Acts.15:23 23:26 Jas.1:1; 
  (b) at parting, farewell: 2 Cor.13:11; 
  (with) on other occasions, be of good cheer: ἐν κυρίῳ, Phil.3:1 4:4 (cf. συν-χαίρω).†
 (AS)

G5464.d:
χάλαζα, -ης, ἡ
 [in LXX chiefly for בָּרָד ;] 
hail: Rev.8:7 11:19 16:21.†
 (AS)

G5466.d:
Χαλδαῖος, -ου, ὁ 
 a Chaldæan: γῆ Χαλδαίων, Acts.7:4.†
 (AS)

G5468.d:
χαλιναγωγέω, -ῶ
 (χαλινός, ἄγω), 
to lead with a bridle; metaphorically, to bridle, restrain: with accusative, γλῶσσαν, Jas.1:26; σῶμα, Jas.3:2.†
 (AS)

G5469.d:
χαλινός, -οῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג ;] 
a bridle: Jas.3:3, Rev.14:20.†
 (AS)

G5470.d:
χάλκεος, -έα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν) 
 (χαλκός), [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;] 
brazen (i.e. of copper): Rev.9:20.†
 (AS)

G5471.d:
χαλκεύς, -έως, ὁ
 (χαλκός), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;] 
a worker, in metal, esp. a copper-smith: 2 Tim.4:14.†
 (AS)

G5472.d:
χαλκηδών, -όνος, ὁ 
 chalcedony, "supposed to denote a green silicate of copper found in the mines near Chalcedon " (Swete): Rev.21:19.†
 (AS)

G5473.d:
χαλκίον, -ου, τό
 (χαλκός), [in LXX: Job.41:22(23) (סִיר), etc. ;] 
a brazen (copper) vessel: Mark.7:4.†
 (AS)

G5474.d:
χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό 
 chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Rev.1:15 2:18 (RV, burnished brass).†
 (AS)

G5475.d:
χαλκός, -oῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;] 
copper: 1 Cor.13:1, Rev.18:12; by meton., of copper coin, Matt.10:9, Mark.6:8 12:41.†
 (AS)

G5476.d:
χαμαί 
 adv., 
on or to the ground: John.9:6 18:6.†
 (AS)

G5477.d:
Χαναάν, ἡ indecl. (Heb. כְּנַעַן), 
 Canaan: Acts.7:11; γῆ Χ., Acts.13:19.†
 (AS)

G5479.d:
χαρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
 (χαίρω), [in LXX for שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן, etc. ;] 
joy, delight: Luke.1:14 15:7, 10, John.15:11 16:22, 24 17:13, Acts.8:8, 2 Cor.1:24 7:13 8:2, Gal.5:22, Col.1:11, Phil.2:2, 1 John.1:4, 2 John.12; opposite to κατήφεια, Jas.4:9; to λύπη, John.16:20; χ. τῆς πίστεως, Phil.1:25; ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι (χαίρειν, which see), χαρᾷ, John.3:29, 1 Pet.1:8; χ. ἔχειν, Phm 7; πληροῦν (-οῦσθαι) χαρᾶς, Acts.13:52, Rom.15:13, 2 Tim.1:4; ποιεῖν χ. μεγάλην, Acts.15:3; ἀπὸ τῆς χ., Matt.13:44, Luke.24:41, Acts.12:14; ἐν χ., Rom.15:32; μετὰ χαρᾶς, Matt.13:20 28:8, Mark.4:16, Luke.8:13 10:17 24:52, Phil.1:4 2:29, Heb.10:34 13:17; id. beforeπνεύματος ἁγίου, 1 Thess.1:6; χ. ἐν π. ἁ, Rom.14:17; χ. ἐπί, 2 Cor.7:4; διά, 1 Thess.3:9; ὅτι, John.16:21; ἵνα, III Jn 4 By meton., of the cause or occasion of joy: Luke.2:10, 2 Cor.1:15, WH, txt., R, mg., Phil.4:1, 1 Thess.2:19-20, Heb.12:2, Jas.1:2; ἡ χ. τ. κυρίου, Matt.25:21, 23.†
 (AS)

G5480.d:
χάραγμα, -τος, τό
 (χαράσσω, to engrave), 
  (a) a stamp, impress, mark: Rev.13:16-17 14:9, 11 16:2 19:20 20:4 (see Deiss., BS, 240 ff.); 
  (b) a thing graven: Acts.17:29.†
 (AS)

G5481.d:
χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
 (χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Lev.13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), 2Ma.4:10, 4Ma.15:4 א R * ;] 
  1. a tool for graving. 
  2. a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaphorically, χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, Heb.1:3.†
 (AS)

G5482.d:
χάραξ, -ακος, ὁ
 (χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר, etc. ;] 
  1. a pointed stake 
  2. a palisade or rampart: Luke.19:43.†
 (AS)

G5483.d:
χαρίζομαι
 (χάρις), [in LXX: Est.8:7 (נָתַן), Sng.1:4 א, Sir.12:3, 2 -4Ma.9:1-32 * ;] 
  1. to show favour or kindness: with dative of person(s), Gal.3:18. 
  2. to give freely, bestow: with accusative and dative, Luke.7:21, Acts.3:14 25:11, 16 27:24, Rom.8:32, 1 Cor.2:12, Phil.1:29 2:9, Phm 22. 
  3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Luke.7:42-43 (EGT, in l); of sin, 2 Cor.2:7 2:10 12:13, Eph.4:32, Col.2:13 3:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).†
 (AS)

G5484.d:
therefore, because of this, for this reason 
the acc. sg form of the noun χάριν which can be used as an improper preposition, on account of, because of, for this reason Lk. 7:47; Eph. 3:1, 14; 1 John. 3:12; for the sake of, in order to, Gal. 3:19; Titus. 1:5, 11; Jude 16; on the score of, 1 Timm. 5:14*

G5485.d:
χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., accusative, χάριν (χάριτα in Acts.24:27, Ju 4; see WH, App., 157), 
 [in LXX chiefly for חֵן ;] 
  1. objectively, that which causes favourable regard, gracefulness, grace, loveliness of form, graciousness of speech (cl.; Ecc.10:12, Sir.21:16, al.): Col.4:6; λόγοι τ. χάριτος (genitive qual.), Luke.4:22. 
  2. Subjectively, 
  (a) on the part of the giver, grace, graciousness, kindness, goodwill, favour: Luke.2:52, Acts.7:10, al.; esp. in NT of the divine favour, grace, with emphasis on its freeness and universality: Luke.1:30, Acts.14:26, Rom.1:7, 1 Cor.1:3, al.; opposite to ὀφείλημα, Rom.4:4, 16; to ἔργα, Rom.11:6; 
  (b) on the part of the receiver, a sense of favour received, thanks, gratitude: Rom.6:17 7:25, al.; χ. ἔχειν, to be thankful, Luke.17:9, 1 Tim.1:12, al. 
  3. Objectively, of the effect of grace, 
  (a) a state of grace: Rom.5:2, 2 Tim.2:1, 1 Pet.5:12, 2 Pet.3:18; 
  (b) a proof or gift of grace (cl., a favour): John.1:16, Acts.6:8, Rom.1:5, 1 Cor.3:10, 2 Cor.9:8, Gal.2:9, Eph.3:2, 1 Pet.5:5, 10 al. (For fuller treatment of the NT usage, see AR, Eph., 221ff.; DB, ii, 254ff.; DCG, i, 686ff.; Cremer, see word). 
 (AS)

G5486.d:
χάρισμα, -τος, τό
 (χαρίζομαι) [in LXX: Sir.7:33 א (AB, χάρις) Sir.38:30 Bl (א AB2R, χρῖσμα) * ;] 
a gift of grace, a free gift, esp. of extra­ordinary operations of the Spirit in the Apostolic Church, but including  all spiritual graces and endowments (Lft., Notes, 148 f.): Rom.1:11 5:15-16 6:23 11:29 12:6, 1 Cor.1:7 7:7 12:4 12:9 12:28 12:30-31, 2 Cor.1:11, 1 Tim.4:14, 2 Tim.1:6, 1 Pet.4:10.†
 (AS)

G5487.d:
χαριτόω, -ῶ
 (χάρις), [in LXX: Sir.18:17 (ἀνδρί κεχαριτωμένῳ; Vg., justificato; Syr., saintly) * ;] 
to endow with χάρις (which see), i.e. 
  1. (a) to make graceful; 
  (b) to make gracious (Sir, l.with). 
  2. In Hellenistic writings (for exx., see AR, Eph., 227; Lft., Notes, 315), 
  (a) to cause to find favour; 
  (b) to endue with grace (i.e. divine favour): Luke.1:28, Eph.1:6.†
 (AS)

G5488.d:
χαρράν 
 indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: Gen.29:4 E, Eze.27:28 B, elsewhere -άν­Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia: Acts.7:2, 4.†
 (AS)

G5489.d:
χάρτης, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Isa.8:1 A, Jer.36:2, 6 36:23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;] 
a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (see Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jn 12 (Plat., Inscr.).†
 (AS)

G5490.d:
χάσμα, -τος, τό
 (χάσκω, to yawn), [in LXX: 2Ki.18:17 (פַּחַת)* ;] 
a chasm, wide space: Luke.16:26.†
 (AS)

G5491.d:
χεῖλος, -ους, τό, genitive pl., -εων (see Bl., § 8, 4; Thackeray, Gr., I, 151), 
 [in LXX chiefly for שָׂפָה ;] 
a lip (as in Heb., of the lip as the organ of speech): Matt.15:8, Mark.7:6, Rom.3:13, 1 Cor.14:21, Heb.13:15, 1 Pet.3:10" (LXX) . Metaphorical, of things, an edge, brink, etc. (Hom., Hdt., al.): of the sea­shore, Heb.11:12.†
 (AS)

G5492.d:
χειμάζω
 (χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pro.26:10 (†) * ;] 
  1. to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters. 
  2. to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Acts.27:18.†
 (AS)

G5493.d:
χείμμαρος (shortened form of the more usual -οος, Attic contr., -ους), -ον 
 (χεῖμα, ῥέω) [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל ;] 
winter-flowing; as subst., ὁ χ. (sc. ποταμός), a torrent: John.18:1.†
 (AS)

G5494.d:
χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ 
 [in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָו ;] 
  1. winter: John.10:22, 2 Tim.4:21; genitive, χειμῶνος, in winter, Matt.24:20, Mark.13:18. 
  2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Matt.16:3 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Acts.27:20.†
 (AS)

G5495.d:
χείρ, genitive, χειρος (accusative, χεῖραν, 1 Pet.5:6 T), ἡ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for יָד ;] 
the hand: Matt.3:12, Mark.3:1, Luke.6:6, al. mult.; ἡ χ., acting subject, Luke.22:21; pl., Acts.17:25 20:34, 1 John.1:1; τ. ἔργα τῶν χ., Acts.7:41, Rev.9:20; ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τ. ἐμῇ χ., 1 Cor.16:21, Col.4:18, 2 Thess.3:17; prepositional phrases, esp. those without art., similar to Heb. constructions (Bl., §32, 4; 40, 9; 46, 9), ἐν χ.; with genitive (Lft., in l.), Gal.3:19; σὺν χ. ἀγγέλου, Acts.7:35; διὰ (τῶν) χειρῶν (διὰ χειρός), Mark.6:2, Acts.5:12 7:25, al.; ἐπὶ χειρῶν, Matt.4:6, Luke.4:11; ellipse of χ. (ἡ δεξία, ἀριστερα; Bl., §44, 1), Matt.6:3, al. By meton., for the power or activity of an individual, Matt.17:22, Mark.9:31, Luke.9:31, John.10:39, Acts.12:11, al.; metaphorically, of the activity or power of God: Luke.1:66 23:46, John.10:29, Acts.11:21 13:11, al. 
 (AS)

G5496.d:
χειραγωγέω, -ῶ
 (χειραγωγός), [in LXX: Jdg.16:26 A (יָד חָזַק), Tob.11:16 א * ;] 
to lead by the hand: Acts.9:8 22:11.†
 (AS)

G5497.d:
χειρ-αγωγός, -όν
 (χείρ, ἄγω) 
leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Acts.13:11.†
 (AS)

G5498.d:
χειρόγραφος, -ον
 (χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: Tob.5:3 9:2, 5 * ;] 
written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaphorically, Col.2:14.†
 (AS)

G5499.d:
χειρο-ποίητος, -ον
 (χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל ;] 
made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, Mark.14:58, Acts.7:48 17:24, Heb.9:11, 24; of circumcision, Eph.2:11.†
 (AS)
